/****************************************************************************
 * RK3576 Gigabit Ethernet MAC (DWC EQOS, "dwmac-4.20a") -- register map.
 *
 * Only the registers this driver touches are listed, and every offset here
 * carries the TRM chapter it came from.  The controller is the Synopsys
 * DWC_ether_qos block, whose register names are the ones the TRM uses:
 *
 *   MAC  registers  0x0000..0x03FF   (configuration, filtering, MDIO)
 *   MTL  registers  0x0D00..0x0D3F   (queue thresholds)
 *   DMA  registers  0x1000..0x117F   (channel 0 only)
 *
 * The MAC's own "GMAC" prefix in the TRM is dropped here to keep the names
 * short; RK3576_GMAC_ prefixes the rest.
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __VENDOR_ROCKCHIP_RK3576_HARDWARE_RK3576_GMAC_H
#define __VENDOR_ROCKCHIP_RK3576_HARDWARE_RK3576_GMAC_H

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <nuttx/config.h>

#include <stdint.h>

/****************************************************************************
 * Pre-processor Definitions
 ****************************************************************************/

/* MAC registers (TRM Part 2, ch. 8.4.3) ***********************************/

#define RK3576_GMAC_MAC_CONFIGURATION  0x0000
#define RK3576_GMAC_MAC_PACKET_FILTER  0x0008
#define RK3576_GMAC_MAC_VERSION        0x0110
#define RK3576_GMAC_MAC_HW_FEATURE0    0x011c
#define RK3576_GMAC_MAC_HW_FEATURE1    0x0120
#define RK3576_GMAC_MAC_MDIO_ADDRESS   0x0200
#define RK3576_GMAC_MAC_MDIO_DATA      0x0204
#define RK3576_GMAC_MAC_ADDRESS0_HIGH  0x0300
#define RK3576_GMAC_MAC_ADDRESS0_LOW   0x0304

/* MAC_CONFIGURATION, 0x0000 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_RE           (1u << 0)  /* Receiver enable      */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_TE           (1u << 1)  /* Transmitter enable   */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_DM           (1u << 13) /* Full duplex          */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_FES          (1u << 14) /* Fast (100M) speed    */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_PS           (1u << 15) /* Port select: 1 = MII */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_JE           (1u << 16) /* Jumbo frame enable   */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_JD           (1u << 17) /* Jabber disable       */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_WD           (1u << 19) /* Watchdog disable     */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_ACS          (1u << 20) /* Auto pad/CRC strip   */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_CST          (1u << 21) /* CRC strip            */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_S2KP         (1u << 22) /* Support 2K packets   */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_GPSLCE       (1u << 23) /* Giant packet limit   */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_IPC          (1u << 27) /* Checksum offload     */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CONFIG_ARPEN        (1u << 31) /* ARP offload          */

/* MAC_PACKET_FILTER, 0x0008.
 *
 * The extracted TRM text loses the bit rows for this register's low bits: the
 * field names run "DBF, PM, DAIF, HMC, HUC, PR" but only four bit rows
 * (3, 2, 1, 0) survive.  PM is the one that matters -- bit 2, "Pass All
 * Multicast", reset 0 -- and every candidate layout agrees neither PM nor PR
 * can break unicast reception, so a wrong guess costs multicast and nothing
 * else.  If IGMP or IPv6 neighbour discovery ever stops working, this is the
 * first register to look at.
 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_FILTER_PR           (1u << 0) /* Promiscuous          */
#define RK3576_GMAC_FILTER_DAIF         (1u << 1) /* DA inverse filter    */
#define RK3576_GMAC_FILTER_PM           (1u << 2) /* Pass all multicast   */
#define RK3576_GMAC_FILTER_DBF          (1u << 3) /* Disable broadcast    */
#define RK3576_GMAC_FILTER_RA           (1u << 31) /* Receive all         */

/* MAC_MDIO_ADDRESS, 0x0200.
 *
 * CR is the CSR-clock divider: MDC = CSR / (2 * (CR + 1)) -- no, the TRM's
 * table is direct: 0000 = /42, 0001 = /62, 0010 = /16, 0011 = /26,
 * 0100 = /102, 0101 = /124, 0110 = /204, 0111 = /324.  /324 keeps MDC inside
 * the PHY's 2.5 MHz ceiling for any CSR clock below ~800 MHz, which is what
 * bring-up wants: reading the PHY must not depend on knowing the CSR rate.
 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_GB     (1u << 0)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_C45E   (1u << 1)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_GOC_S  2
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_GOC_M  (3u << 2)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_GOC_WRITE (1u << 2)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_GOC_READ  (3u << 2)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_SKAP   (1u << 4)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_CR_S   8
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_CR_M   (0xfu << 8)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_CR_324 (7u << 8)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_NTC_S  12
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_RDA_S  16
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_PA_S   21
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_BTB    (1u << 26)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_ADDRESS_PSE    (1u << 27)

#define RK3576_GMAC_MDIO_DATA_GD_M     0x0000ffff

/* MAC_ADDRESS0_HIGH / _LOW, 0x0300 / 0x0304 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_ADDR_HIGH_AE        (1u << 31) /* Address enable       */
#define RK3576_GMAC_ADDR_HIGH_M         0x0000ffff
#define RK3576_GMAC_ADDR_LOW_M          0xffffffff

/* MTL registers (TRM Part 2, ch. 8.5) *************************************/

#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_TXQ0_OPERATION_MODE 0x0d00
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_RXQ0_OPERATION_MODE 0x0d30

/* MTL_TXQ0_OPERATION_MODE, 0x0D00 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_TXQ0_FTQ        (1u << 0)  /* Flush TX queue       */
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_TXQ0_TSF        (1u << 1)  /* Store and forward    */
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_TXQ0_TXQEN_S    2
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_TXQ0_TXQEN_M    (3u << 2)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_TXQ0_TXQEN_ENABLE (2u << 2)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_TXQ0_TTC_S      4
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_TXQ0_TQS_S      16
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_TXQ0_TQS_M      (0x3fu << 16)

/* MTL_RXQ0_OPERATION_MODE, 0x0D30 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_RXQ0_RSF        (1u << 5)  /* Store and forward    */
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_RXQ0_DIS_TCP_EF (1u << 6)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_RXQ0_EHFC       (1u << 7)  /* HW flow control      */
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_RXQ0_RFA_S      8
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_RXQ0_RFA_M      (0x3fu << 8)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_RXQ0_RFD_S      14
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_RXQ0_RFD_M      (0x3fu << 14)
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_RXQ0_RQS_S      20
#define RK3576_GMAC_MTL_RXQ0_RQS_M      (0x7fu << 20)

/* DMA registers (TRM Part 2, ch. 8.6).  Only channel 0 is used: the DTB
 * instantiates queue0 alone, so channels 1..7 are never touched.
 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_MODE                0x1000
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_SYSBUS_MODE         0x1004
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_INTERRUPT_STATUS    0x1008
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_CH0_CONTROL         0x1100
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_CH0_TX_CONTROL      0x1104
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_CH0_RX_CONTROL      0x1108
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_CH0_TXDESC_LIST_ADDR 0x1114
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_CH0_RXDESC_LIST_ADDR 0x111c
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_CH0_TXDESC_TAIL_PTR 0x1120
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_CH0_RXDESC_TAIL_PTR 0x1128
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_CH0_TXDESC_RING_LEN 0x112c
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_CH0_RXDESC_RING_LEN 0x1130
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_CH0_INTERRUPT_ENABLE 0x1134
#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_CH0_STATUS          0x1160

/* DMA_MODE, 0x1000 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_DMA_MODE_SWR        (1u << 0)  /* Software reset       */

/* DMA_SYSBUS_MODE, 0x1004.  Only the burst lengths the vendor DTB names
 * (blen = 4/8/16) are programmed; the AXI outstanding-request limits it also
 * names are left at their reset values, because the extracted TRM text
 * interleaves that field's bit rows with its neighbours' and a wrong guess
 * there buys nothing but a mystery.
 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_SYSBUS_BLEN4        (1u << 1)
#define RK3576_GMAC_SYSBUS_BLEN8        (1u << 2)
#define RK3576_GMAC_SYSBUS_BLEN16       (1u << 3)
#define RK3576_GMAC_SYSBUS_EAME         (1u << 18) /* AXI master error rsp */

/* DMA_CH0_CONTROL, 0x1100 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0CTRL_PBLX8       (1u << 16) /* 8x programmable burst */

/* DMA_CH0_TX_CONTROL, 0x1104 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0TX_ST            (1u << 0)  /* Start transmission   */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0TX_OSP           (1u << 4)  /* Operate on 2nd pkt   */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0TX_TXPBL_S       16
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0TX_TXPBL_M       (0x3fu << 16)

/* DMA_CH0_RX_CONTROL, 0x1108 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0RX_SR            (1u << 0)  /* Start receive        */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0RX_RBSZ_S        1
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0RX_RBSZ_M        (0x3fffu << 1)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0RX_RXPBL_S       16
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0RX_RXPBL_M       (0x3fu << 16)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0RX_RPF           (1u << 31) /* Rx packet flush      */

/* DMA_CH0_INTERRUPT_ENABLE, 0x1134.
 *
 * The interrupt-status bits, and please read this before changing them.
 *
 * The TRM puts the two summary enables at bits 15 (NIE) and 14 (AIE), and
 * says bits 31:16 of this register are read-only.  The DWC databook the
 * mainline stmmac driver was written against puts them one bit higher, at 16
 * and 15.  Both documents describe the same block, and nothing in the tree
 * can settle it without hardware, so the driver writes *both* candidate
 * positions: whichever is real takes effect, and the other is either the
 * neighbouring summary enable or a read-only reserved bit.
 *
 * The individual bits (TIE 0, RIE 6, RBUE 7, FBE 12) agree in both
 * documents and are what the handler actually acts on.
 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_TIE          (1u << 0)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_TBUE         (1u << 2)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_RIE          (1u << 6)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_RBUE         (1u << 7)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_RSE          (1u << 8)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_RWTE         (1u << 9)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_ETIE         (1u << 10)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_ERIE         (1u << 11)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_FBEE         (1u << 12)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_CDEE         (1u << 13)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_AIE_TRM      (1u << 14)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_NIE_TRM      (1u << 15)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_AIE_DATABOOK (1u << 15)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0INT_NIE_DATABOOK (1u << 16)

/* DMA_CH0_STATUS, 0x1160.  Write 1 to clear. */

#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_TI           (1u << 0)  /* Transmit complete    */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_TBU          (1u << 2)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_RI           (1u << 6)  /* Receive complete     */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_RBU          (1u << 7)  /* Rx buffer unavailable */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_RPS          (1u << 8)  /* Rx process stopped   */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_RWT          (1u << 9)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_ETI          (1u << 10)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_ERI          (1u << 11)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_FBE          (1u << 12) /* Fatal bus error      */
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_CDE          (1u << 13)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_AIS          (1u << 14)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_NIS          (1u << 15)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_AIS_DATABOOK (1u << 15)
#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_NIS_DATABOOK (1u << 16)

/* Every bit a completed transfer sets; the handler reaps on these alone. */

#define RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_ERRORS                                        \
  (RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_FBE | RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_CDE |                     \
   RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_ERI | RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_RPS |                     \
   RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_RWT | RK3576_GMAC_CH0STS_ERI)

/* DMA_INTERRUPT_STATUS, 0x1008: bit 16 is "channel 0 has a pending
 * interrupt", which the DMA raises on the OR of the channel's status bits.
 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_DMAINT_DC0IS        (1u << 16)

/* Descriptors (TRM Part 2, ch. 8.6.3 and 8.6.8) **************************
 *
 * Four 32-bit words.  TX read format:  des0 = buffer 1 address,
 * des2[13:0] = buffer 1 length, des3 = control/status.  RX read format:
 * des0 = buffer 1 address, des3 = control/status.  The same words are
 * written back by the DMA, which clears OWN and puts the received frame
 * length in des3[14:0].
 */

#define RK3576_GMAC_DESC_SIZE   16

#define RK3576_GMAC_TDES3_OWN   (1u << 31)
#define RK3576_GMAC_TDES3_CTXT  (1u << 30)
#define RK3576_GMAC_TDES3_FD    (1u << 29)
#define RK3576_GMAC_TDES3_LD    (1u << 28)
#define RK3576_GMAC_TDES3_FL_M  0x00007fff

#define RK3576_GMAC_RDES3_OWN   (1u << 31)
#define RK3576_GMAC_RDES3_IOC   (1u << 30)
#define RK3576_GMAC_RDES3_BUF2V (1u << 25)
#define RK3576_GMAC_RDES3_BUF1V (1u << 24)
#define RK3576_GMAC_RDES3_PL_M  0x00007fff
#define RK3576_GMAC_RDES3_ES    (1u << 15)

/* SDGMAC_GRF (TRM Part 1, ch. 5.15) **************************************
 *
 * The GMACn_CON registers are hiword-write-enable: bits [31:16] gate the
 * write of the corresponding bit in [15:0].
 */

#define RK3576_SDGMAC_GRF_GMAC0_CON     0x0020
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_GRF_GMAC1_CON     0x0024
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_GRF_GMAC_CON(n)   (0x0020 + (n) * 4)

#define RK3576_SDGMAC_CON_CLK_GATING_EN (1u << 0) /* 1 = gate, 0 = clock on */
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_CON_SBD_FLOWCTRL_S 1
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_CON_SBD_FLOWCTRL_M (3u << 1)
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_CON_RMII_MODE     (1u << 3) /* 1 = RMII, 0 = RGMII    */
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_CON_RMII_CLK_GATE (1u << 4)
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_CON_TXCLK_DIV_S   5
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_CON_TXCLK_DIV_M   (3u << 5)
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_CON_TXCLK_DIV_2P5M (2u << 5)
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_CON_TXCLK_DIV_25M  (3u << 5)
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_CON_TXCLK_DIV_125M (0u << 5)
#define RK3576_SDGMAC_CON_TXCLK_SEL     (1u << 7) /* 0 = CRU, 1 = IO pad   */

/* WRITE_EN(n) builds the hiword write-enable mask for a field at [n] or
 * below: every bit set in HIWORD covers the same bit in the low half.
 */

#define RK3576_SDGMAC_HIWORD(v)         ((uint32_t)(v) << 16)

/* VCCIO_IOC RGMII delay lines (TRM Part 1, ch. 5.9) ***********************
 *
 * One register per controller *and per pin group*; the KICKPI-K7 uses pin
 * group m0 for both ports, so only MISC_CON2 and MISC_CON4 are ever written.
 * Same layout in each, also hiword-write-enable:
 *
 *   [15]     rxclk_delay_ena
 *   [14:8]   rxclk_delayline_num
 *   [7]      txclk_delay_ena
 *   [6:0]    txclk_delayline_num
 */

#define RK3576_VCCIO_IOC_MISC_CON2      0x0408 /* GMAC0, pin group m0 */
#define RK3576_VCCIO_IOC_MISC_CON3      0x040c /* GMAC0, pin group m1 */
#define RK3576_VCCIO_IOC_MISC_CON4      0x0410 /* GMAC1, pin group m0 */
#define RK3576_VCCIO_IOC_MISC_CON5      0x0414 /* GMAC1, pin group m1 */

#define RK3576_VCCIO_DLY_TX_ENA        (1u << 7)
#define RK3576_VCCIO_DLY_TX_NUM_S      0
#define RK3576_VCCIO_DLY_TX_NUM_M      (0x7fu << 0)
#define RK3576_VCCIO_DLY_RX_ENA        (1u << 15)
#define RK3576_VCCIO_DLY_RX_NUM_S      8
#define RK3576_VCCIO_DLY_RX_NUM_M      (0x7fu << 8)

#define RK3576_VCCIO_DLY_HIWORD(v)     ((uint32_t)(v) << 16)

#endif /* __VENDOR_ROCKCHIP_RK3576_HARDWARE_RK3576_GMAC_H */

/****************************************************************************
 * RK3576 Gigabit Ethernet MAC (DWC EQOS) driver.
 *
 * The driver owns everything that belongs to the controller: the CRU clocks,
 * the SDGMAC_GRF RGMII mode registers, the VCCIO RGMII delay lines, the MDIO
 * bus and the PHY state machine, the descriptor rings, and the netdev lower
 * half.  What it does *not* own is what belongs to the board: which pins carry
 * the RGMII signals, and the PHY reset line.  Those come in through the
 * configuration structure below, which the board layer fills in.
 *
 * Two instances, one file, from the first line: GMAC0 and GMAC1 are separate
 * controllers with separate MDIO buses, and nothing but the CRU gate register
 * and the clock tree is shared.
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __VENDOR_ROCKCHIP_CHIPS_RK3576_RK3576_GMAC_H
#define __VENDOR_ROCKCHIP_CHIPS_RK3576_RK3576_GMAC_H

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <nuttx/config.h>

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef CONFIG_RK3576_GMAC

/* Controller instance indices, used as the first argument of
 * rk3576_gmac_initialize().  They index the CRU clock names, the base
 * addresses, the interrupt numbers and the SDGMAC_GRF/VCCIO registers, so
 * they are the controller index and not the port number.
 */

#define RK3576_GMAC0 0
#define RK3576_GMAC1 1

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Types
 ****************************************************************************/

/* Everything the driver needs to know about the board's port.
 *
 * The RGMII delay taps and the PHY address are board facts that cannot be
 * discovered at run time: the taps come from the vendor DTB and the PHY
 * address from the board's strap resistors, so both are passed in rather
 * than probed and guessed.  The two callbacks are the board's half of the
 * bring-up: pinmuxing the fourteen RGMII pads, and driving the PHY's reset
 * line.
 */

struct rk3576_gmac_config_s
{
  /* RGMII delay lines, in 1/8 ns taps.  VCCIO_IOC MISC_CON offset differs
   * per controller *and* per pin group; the board passes the offset of the
   * group it actually muxed.
   */

  uint16_t ioc_offset;
  uint8_t tx_delay;
  uint8_t rx_delay;
  bool tx_delay_ena;
  bool rx_delay_ena;

  /* First MDIO address to try.  The MAE0621A answers at two addresses (its
   * strap pins select 1, and PHYAD_0 defaults to enabled so it also answers
   * at 0), so the driver probes this one, then 0, then scans.
   */

  uint8_t phyaddr;

  /* The port's own MAC address.  Nothing on this board supplies one -- no
   * DTB property, no OTP -- so it is a board decision and it must be in
   * place before the interface is brought up.
   */

  FAR const uint8_t *mac;

  /* Board callbacks.  Both may be NULL if the board has nothing to do. */

  CODE int (*pinmux)(void);
  CODE void (*phy_reset)(bool assert);
};

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Function Prototypes
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rk3576_gmac_initialize
 *
 * Description:
 *   Bring the platform layer up (clocks, SDGMAC_GRF, RGMII delays, controller
 *   reset), verify that the controller answers, probe the PHY over MDIO, and
 *   register the netdev -- but do not start the DMA rings.  Those come up in
 *   ifup, on the thread that runs `ifup eth0`.
 *
 *   Called once per controller, from board_late_initialize().
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   intf - RK3576_GMAC0 or RK3576_GMAC1
 *   cfg  - board description of this port (see above); copied, not retained
 *          as a pointer, so a `static const` in the board file is fine.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   OK on success, a negated errno on failure.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int rk3576_gmac_initialize(int intf,
                           FAR const struct rk3576_gmac_config_s *cfg);

#endif /* CONFIG_RK3576_GMAC */
#endif /* __VENDOR_ROCKCHIP_CHIPS_RK3576_RK3576_GMAC_H */

* Description:
 *   Invalidate the data cache within the specified region; we will be
 *   performing a DMA operation in this region and we want to purge old data
 *   in the cache.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   start - virtual start address of region
 *   end   - virtual end address of region + 1
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   None
 *
 * Assumptions:
 *   This operation is not atomic.  This function assumes that the caller
 *   has exclusive access to the address range so that no harm is done if
 *   the operation is pre-empted.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void up_invalidate_dcache(uintptr_t start, uintptr_t end)
{
  arm64_dcache_range(start, end, CACHE_OP_INVD);
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: up_invalidate_dcache_all
 *
 * Description:

 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   None
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   None
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void up_invalidate_dcache_all(void)
{
  arm64_dcache_all(CACHE_OP_INVD);
}

config RK3576_GMAC
	bool "Gigabit Ethernet MAC (DWC EQOS, GMAC0 + GMAC1)"
	default n
	depends on NET && NET_ETHERNET
	select SCHED_WORKQUEUE
	select SCHED_LPWORK
	---help---
		Enable the RK3576 Gigabit Ethernet MAC driver: the two Synopsys
		DWC EQOS controllers at 0x2a220000 (GMAC0) and 0x2a230000
		(GMAC1).  Each has its own MDIO bus and its own RGMII PHY; the
		two share nothing but the CRU gate register and the clock tree.

		The driver is a netdev lower half (netdev_lowerhalf): the
		descriptor rings point straight at the packet buffers the network
		stack owns, so a frame is not copied in either direction.
		Everything that belongs to the SoC is here -- the CRU clocks, the
		SDGMAC_GRF RGMII mode registers, the VCCIO delay lines, the
		controller reset, MDIO, the PHY state machine and the rings.  The
		parts that belong to the board -- which pads carry the RGMII
		signals and which GPIO resets which PHY -- come in through
		rk3576_gmac_initialize().

		CONFIG_IOB_BUFSIZE must be at least 1518 and a whole AXI beat (a
		multiple of 16), because the RX buffer size programmed into the
		DMA is the network buffer size itself.  The ethernet board
		configuration uses 1536; the driver refuses to build otherwise.

if RK3576_GMAC

config RK3576_GMAC_RX_DESC
	int "Receive descriptor ring depth"
	default 16
	range 4 64
	---help---
		Number of receive descriptors, which is also the receive quota:
		one netpkt is held per slot for as long as the interface is up,
		out of CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS.  Each port claims this many, so a
		two-port build holds twice as many.

config RK3576_GMAC_TX_DESC
	int "Transmit descriptor ring depth"
	default 8
	range 4 64
	---help---
		Number of transmit descriptors, which is also the transmit quota.
		A packet stays in its slot, and in the network buffer pool, until
		the DMA has sent it.

config KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET
	bool "On-board dual Gigabit Ethernet (GMAC0 + GMAC1)"
	default n
	depends on RK3576_GMAC && RK3576_GPIO
	---help---
		Bring up the two on-board RJ45 ports, each behind its own Maxio
		MAE0621A gigabit PHY:

		  GMAC0 (0x2a220000) -- MAE0621A -- RJ45
		  GMAC1 (0x2a230000) -- MAE0621A -- RJ45

		This is a board function, not a peripheral that has to be added:
		both PHYs are populated on every revision of the board.

		The pin sets are disjoint -- GMAC0 on GPIO bank 3 at alternate
		function 3 (the eth0m0 group), GMAC1 on bank 2 at function 2
		(eth1m0) -- which is what makes two instances safe at the pinmux
		level.  The PHY reset lines are crossed with respect to the data
		pins: GMAC0's data is on bank 3 but its reset is GPIO2_B5, and
		GMAC1's is the other way round (GPIO3_A3).

		Both ports are RGMII with the TXC driven by the SoC
		(clock_in_out = "output") and the PHY adding the RX delay in its
		own pins (rgmii-rxid).  That is a fact rather than a preference:
		the PHYs are strapped TXDLY = 0, RXDLY = 1, and the resistors
		that would have fed the PHY's 125 MHz CLKOUT back to the SoC are
		marked NC and unpopulated.  So the SoC supplies the TX delay and
		must leave its RX delay off, or the delay is counted twice.

if KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET

config KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_PORT1
	bool "Also bring up the second port (GMAC1)"
	default y
	---help---
		Register the second RJ45 as well.  Turning this off leaves only
		GMAC0, which is useful when only one port's PHY is suspected: it
		halves the network buffers the driver holds.

config KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_TX_DELAY0
	int "GMAC0 RGMII TX delay (taps, 1/8 ns each)"
	default 33
	range 0 127
	---help---
		The tx_delay the vendor DTB specifies for ethernet@2a220000: 0x21,
		i.e. 33 taps of the VCCIO TX clock delay line.  A number here, not
		a register write somewhere in the driver, so that retiming a board
		is a rebuild and not an edit.

		The PHY's own TXDLY strap is 0 on this board, so this is the only
		TX delay in the path.  If the link trains at gigabit but loses
		frames, this is the first number to move.

config KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_TX_DELAY1
	int "GMAC1 RGMII TX delay (taps, 1/8 ns each)"
	default 32
	range 0 127
	---help---
		The tx_delay the vendor DTB specifies for ethernet@2a230000: 0x20,
		i.e. 32 taps.  One tap less than port 0, which is what the vendor
		DTB says and not a transcription error.

config KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_MACADDR0
	string "GMAC0 MAC address"
	default "02:52:4b:37:76:00"
	---help---
		The address programmed into MAC address register 0 of GMAC0.

		Nothing on this board supplies one: the vendor DTB sets no
		mac-address, no nvmem-cells and no local-mac-address on either
		ethernet node, and the RK3576 GMAC has no OTP MAC.  So the board
		states it.  The default is locally administered (the 0x02 bit) and
		unique per port; give each board its own if several share a
		segment.

	---help---

# So the payload is a packet's worth rather than a fifth of one, and the
# product is what matters: 1516 bytes is one full Ethernet payload, so the
# same 64 buffers now hold 97 KB -- six of today's frames, or more than a
# worst-case 64 KB segment -- for 85 KB more RAM than before.  Raising the
# count instead would work too, but it would take 85 buffers for a single
# frame and leave the pool unable to hold one; this way a buffer is always
# something that can be sent.
#
# This configuration moves both numbers, and both moves belong to the wired
# ports rather than to the camera.
#
# The size becomes 1536 because the GMAC's receive descriptor points straight
# at the buffer: the value programmed into the DMA as the buffer size *is*
# CONFIG_IOB_BUFSIZE, so it has to be a whole AXI beat and hold a full frame.
# 1516 holds the frame but is not a multiple of 16, and the driver refuses to
# build on a size that is not.  1536 is both, and the 20 extra bytes cost
# 2.5 KB over the whole pool.
#
# The count becomes 128 because a wired port holds one buffer per receive
# descriptor for as long as the interface is up: 16 receive plus 8 transmit
# per port, two ports, is 48 of them held permanently, against the 32 the
# stack is warned about consuming.  With 64 the warning would fire and the
# camera's TCP read-ahead would be drawing from what is left; with 128 there
# are 80 left for everything else.
CONFIG_IOB_BUFSIZE=1536
CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS=128

#
# Wired Ethernet: the two on-board RJ45 ports, each behind its own MAE0621A.
#
# This is what the configuration is named for.  The camera half above is kept
# because the board's product is the camera: this is the configuration the
# branch boots, with both wired ports added to it, rather than a stripped build
# that can only prove the MAC works.
#
# The ports are up only after `ifup eth0` and `ifup eth1`: registration and
# the platform bring-up happen at boot, and they print what they found --
# the MAC version (0x00003051 when the block is powered, clocked and un-gated),
# the RGMII delay registers' readback, and which MDIO address the PHY answered
# at.  Nothing here starts the DMA, because that belongs to the thread that can
# sleep.
#

CONFIG_RK3576_GMAC=y
CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET=y
CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_PORT1=y

# The TX delay taps are the vendor DTB's numbers (0x21 and 0x20), and they are
# named here rather than left to the Kconfig defaults for the same reason the
# encoder's self-tests are: a default can change quietly, and retiming a board
# is then an edit rather than a rebuild.  The RX delay is off in both, because
# the PHYs are strapped RXDLY = 1 and adding the SoC's delay on top would count
# it twice.
CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_TX_DELAY0=33
CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_TX_DELAY1=32

# Nothing on this board supplies a MAC address -- no DTB property, no OTP -- so
# these two are the board's statement.  Locally administered, unique per port.
CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_MACADDR0="02:52:4b:37:76:00"
CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_MACADDR1="02:52:4b:37:76:01"

| `CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_MACADDR0` / `1` | board | default `02:52:4b:37:76:00` / `:01` |

Both ports are enabled in `configs/ethernet`, which is the branch's main
configuration (camera half included, unchanged).

### Two things this configuration changed about the IOB pool

`CONFIG_IOB_BUFSIZE` 1516 → **1536** and `CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS` 64 → **128**,
both in `configs/ethernet` only.

- The buffer size because the RX descriptor points straight at the netpkt's
  data area: the value programmed as RBSZ *is* `CONFIG_IOB_BUFSIZE`, so it has
  to hold a full frame and be a whole AXI beat. 1516 is not a multiple of 16;
  the driver `#error`s on a size that is not.
- The count because 16 RX + 8 TX per port × 2 ports = 48 buffers held for the
  life of the interfaces, against a warning line of 64 (`NETPKT_BUFNUM / 2`).
  With 128 there are 80 left for TCP read-ahead and the SV6621.

`.bss` grew 306 KB → 407 KB; `nuttx.bin` 1.92 MB → 1.96 MB, against a 4 MB
firmware slot (`nboot-release.json`, `vendor_fit_size`).

### Where the driver departs from this plan, and why

1. **One descriptor per cache line (64-byte stride).** Descriptors are 16
   bytes, so four share a line and a clean or invalidate on one would touch
   its neighbours' OWN bits. With one per line every cache operation is exact,
   for 3 KB of ring space per port. The rule that makes re-reading a
   not-yet-complete descriptor safe: clean the line before handing it over, so
   a later invalidate can only drop a stale copy.
2. **The interrupt summary enables are written twice.** The TRM puts NIE/AIE
   at bits 15/14; the DWC databook mainline stmmac was written against puts
   them at 16/15. Nothing in the tree can settle that without hardware, so the
   driver sets both candidate positions and acts only on the individual bits
   (TIE 0, RIE 6, RBUE 7, FBE 12), which both documents agree on. If the first
   flash shows link up but no packets, this is the first suspect.
3. **`DMA_SYSBUS_MODE` programs only BLEN4/8/16.** The DTB's `wr_osr_lmt=4`
   and `rd_osr_lmt=8` are left at their reset values: the extracted TRM text
   interleaves that field's bit rows with its neighbours', so a guess buys
   nothing but a mystery.
4. **Multicast is accepted wholesale** (`MAC_PACKET_FILTER.PM`), so
   `addmac`/`rmmac` succeed without touching the hash table — the frame is
   already being received. The low bits of that register are one of the places
   the TRM text extracts badly; PM at bit 2 is the reading that cannot break
   unicast either way, and IGMP/IPv6-ND is what would show it if wrong.
5. **The soft reset uses the two per-port CRU bits only** (`aresetn` and
   `presetn` for the port), not the shared `sdgmac_biu`/`sdgmac_grf` bits. The
   `aresetn` pair is what the DTB's reset ids confirm; the `presetn` pair is
   the TRM's reading of "when high, reset relative logic". If the controller
   answers with version 0, dropping `presetn` is the first thing to try, and
   the code says so.
6. **The RX path allocates a replacement buffer before handing the frame up**,
   and if `netpkt_alloc()` fails it leaves the descriptor alone, stalls the
   ring and re-arms it from a delayed work item. A stalled ring generates no
   interrupts, so without that retry the port would go silently dead the first
   time the IOB pool ran dry.

### Still open, in the order they will bite

1. **Is the controller powered?** `PD_SDGMAC` (memory item 1 above). The boot
   log's `gmac0: version 0x…` answers it: `0x00003051` means yes, `0x00000000`
   means the block is dark and no driver change helps.
2. **Is the 125 MHz clock 125 MHz?** The CRU divider is off CPLL and CPLL's
   rate is whatever the bootloader left. `clk_set_rate(..., 125000000)` +
   readback is logged; if the divider cannot reach it the driver says so
   loudly but still registers, so the port is visible rather than absent.
3. **Does the summary-enable guess hold?** See departure 2.
4. **Do the taps train gigabit?** 33/32 from the DTB; retime by rebuild via
   the two board Kconfig ints.
5. The phase 4-7 work (RX, TX, port 1, 100M/10M, `ifdown`/`ifup`) is written
   but unexercised.

The next flash is the phase 1+2 verdict: `gmac0/1: version`, the SDGMAC_GRF and
VCCIO readbacks, `phy addr N bmsr 0x…`, `registered as eth0/eth1`, and eMMC/SDIO
still working. `ifup eth0` then adds the autonegotiation and link lines.

# configs — 项目功能配置

本目录存放**非 BSP 必须**的功能配置，即那些依赖外部硬件或特定项目场景的 defconfig。

## 与 `boards/.../configs/` 的区别

| | `boards/.../configs/` | `configs/`（本目录） |
|---|---|---|
| **定位** | BSP 配置（板子本身能跑的功能） | 项目功能配置（需要额外硬件或特定场景） |
| **示例** | nsh、ADB、SD 卡、emmc | 屏幕驱动、传感器扩展、创意 Demo |
| **特点** | 单靠这块板子就能用 | 通常绑定特定外设或应用场景 |

## 为什么单独放？

1. **硬件互斥**：某些外设共用引脚（如 FSPI 与 SD 卡槽），一个 defconfig 无法同时包含
2. **职责清晰**：BSP 只描述"板子有什么"（能力下限），本目录描述"我们要用这块板子做什么"（组合了 BSP 能力与项目功能的某个具体场景）
3. **便于维护**：功能配置独立管理，改 A 不影响 B

> 本目录中的每个配置通常**会组合启用 BSP 能力、测试程序与项目功能**，因此它允许超出板子最小能力边界的配置；具体每个配置的定位见各自目录下的 README。

## 使用方法（以dev为例）

```bash
# 使用本目录下的配置编译
./build.sh contest2026_062_PharosTech/configs/dev

# 或者使用cmake
./build.sh contest2026_062_PharosTech/configs/dev --cmake
```
## 注意事项

### 新增配置时务必创建 Make.defs 软链接

Makefile 模式下，`configure.sh` 会在配置目录中查找 `Make.defs`。由于本目录位于 `boards/` 之外，必须手动创建指向板级 `scripts/Make.defs` 的符号链接，否则 Makefile 模式编译会报错 `File Make.defs could not be found`。

```bash
# 在新建的配置目录中创建软链接
ln -s ../../boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/scripts/Make.defs configs/<新配置名>/Make.defs
```

CMake 模式不需要此链接，但 Makefile 模式必须有。

# the MAC version (0x00003051 when the block is powered, clocked and un-gated),

# at.  Nothing here starts the DMA, because that belongs to the thread that can
# sleep.
#

CONFIG_RK3576_GMAC=y

CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_PORT1=y

# The TX delay taps are the vendor DTB's numbers (0x21 and 0x20), and they are
# named here rather than left to the Kconfig defaults for the same reason the
# encoder's self-tests are: a default can change quietly, and retiming a board
# is then an edit rather than a rebuild.  The RX delay is off in both, because
# the PHYs are strapped RXDLY = 1 and adding the SoC's delay on top would count
# it twice.

CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_TX_DELAY1=32

# Nothing on this board supplies a MAC address -- no DTB property, no OTP -- so
# these two are the board's statement.  Locally administered, unique per port.

CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET_MACADDR1="02:52:4b:37:76:01"

# operation is compiled under.

## 新增文件

| 文件 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| [rk3576_gmac.c](contest2026_062_PharosTech/chips/rk3576/rk3576_gmac.c) (2085 行) | 驱动本体:platform 层(CRU 时钟、SDGMAC_GRF、VCCIO 延时线、软复位)、MDIO + PHY 状态机、双向描述符环 + 中断、netdev lowerhalf 适配层 |
| [rk3576_gmac.h](contest2026_062_PharosTech/chips/rk3576/rk3576_gmac.h) | `struct rk3576_gmac_config_s` + `rk3576_gmac_initialize(intf, cfg)` |
| [hardware/rk3576_gmac.h](contest2026_062_PharosTech/chips/rk3576/hardware/rk3576_gmac.h) | 只收录有 TRM 锚点的寄存器(MAC/MTL/DMA、GMACn_CON、VCCIO 延时、描述符格式) |
| [kickpi_k7_ethernet.c](contest2026_062_PharosTech/boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/src/kickpi_k7_ethernet.c) | 两组 14 脚 pinmux 表、两条 PHY 复位线、每口 board 配置 |
| [configs/ethernet/](contest2026_062_PharosTech/configs/ethernet/defconfig) | 本分支主配置:camera 配置 + 两个有线口 |

## 关键取舍

- **描述符一条占一个 cache line(64B 步长)。** 16 字节的描述符四个共用一行,cache clean/invalidate 会碰到邻居的 OWN 位;一条一行后每次维护都是精确的,代价是每口 3 KB 环空间。
- **中断 summary 使能位写了两份。** TRM 说 NIE/AIE 在 bit 15/14,DWC databook(mainline stmmac)说在 16/15。两个候选位都写,handler 只依赖两份文档一致的单个位(TIE 0 / RIE 6 / RBUE 7 / FBE 12)。首次上板若"link up 但无包",先查这里。
- **RX 路径先申请替换缓冲再上交帧;申请失败就让环停住,用延时 work 重试。** 停住的环不再产生中断,没有这个重试,IOB 池一枯竭网口就会静默死掉。
- **multicast 整包放行(PM)**,因此 `addmac/rmmac` 直接成功——帧早已被接收。该寄存器低位的 TRM 文本抽取是坏的,bit 2 是两种解读下都不会破坏单播的读法。
- **软复位只动两个 per-port 位**(`aresetn`/`presetn`),不碰与另一口及 GRF 共享的 `sdgmac_biu/grf` 位;代码注释写明了若版本号读回 0 该先去掉哪个位。

## 与 memory 计划的差异(已回写)

Kconfig 名字没有沿用计划里的 `RK3576_GMAC0/1`、`RK3576_GMAC_TX_DELAY_*`:板级事实放进板级 Kconfig,即 `KICKPI_K7_ETHERNET`、`_PORT1`、`_TX_DELAY0/1`(33/32)、`_MACADDR0/1`;芯片侧只留 `RK3576_GMAC` 与两个环深度。`CONFIG_IOB_BUFSIZE` 1516→1536、`IOB_NBUFFERS` 64→128 只改在新配置里(RBSZ 就是 `IOB_BUFSIZE`,必须是完整 AXI beat;两口 48 个缓冲要长期占用)。这些都记在 [gmac-bringup.md](.dsh/memory/gmac-bringup.md) 末尾新增的 "Implementation status"。

两种构建系统的镜像都改了(chip `CMakeLists.txt`/`Make.defs`、board `src/CMakeLists.txt`/`src/Makefile`),并按 AGENTS 要求在每处加了 `Mirror:` 注释;`rk3576_addrenv.c` 的编译条件也加上了 `CONFIG_RK3576_GMAC`(描述符要 VA→PA)。

## 构建验证

```sh
./build.sh contest2026_062_PharosTech/configs/ethernet --cmake   # → cmake_out/..._ethernet/nuttx.bin, 1.96 MB
./build.sh contest2026_062_PharosTech/configs/camera   --cmake   # 回归,仍通过
```

`rk3576_gmac_initialize`、`netdev_lower_register` 均在 ELF 中;`.bss` 306 KB→407 KB,firmware slot 4 MB 内。

目前仍是"编译通过、从未运行"。flash 后串口应先给 phase 1+2 的结论:`gmac0/1: version 0x00003051`(为 0 则 PD_SDGMAC 没开)、SDGMAC_GRF 与 VCCIO 的回读、`phy addr 1 bmsr 0x…`、`registered as eth0/eth1`,以及 eMMC/SDIO 仍正常。之后 `ifup eth0` 才会重启自协商并打印 `link up 1000M full`。

最大的未知仍是 PD_SDGMAC 供电和 125 MHz 分频能否从 CPLL 得到(驱动会大声打印实际频率但不会因此拒绝注册,以免"没有接口"掩盖真实原因)。

The board reports:
- 125 MHz clock works ✓ (so CPLL divides to 125 MHz, clocks enabled — that means the clock tree and gating worked!)
- `gmac0: DMA software reset never completed` — DMA_MODE.SWR never self-clears.

Notably missing: the "SDGMAC_GRF mode" and "VCCIO RGMII delay" readback logs (those only print when the value changes: `if (before != after)`). And no "version" line — because gm_reset fails before the version read.

Wait: `gm_reset` polls for `DMA_MODE.SWR == 0`. If the register read returns 0 (block not clocked/not responding), the loop would exit immediately with OK. Instead SWR *stays 1* — meaning the write landed and the bit didn't self-clear. So the register block IS accessible and the write is visible. That means:
- The APB/AXI access works → clocks (aclk/pclk) and the CRU reset worked.
- The DMA's internal reset never completes → the DMA isn't running, most likely because the **DMA's own clock** (the `stmmaceth`/125M clock? no, the DMA runs on aclk) ... Hmm.

Key insight: `DMA_MODE.SWR` self-clears only when the DMA has its clocks. In DWC EQOS, the DMA software reset needs `clk_tx_i`/`clk_rx_i`? No — actually the databook says the SWR bit "is cleared only after all the DMA CSR registers are reset... the reset is complete only if the clocks to the DMA are running." Specifically, for DWC_ether_qos, SWR requires the *MAC* clock domains to be alive. Hmm.

Let me think about what's actually wrong:

Possibility 1: **DMA_MODE itself isn't the register at 0x1000.** If 0x1000 were not DMA_MODE but something else writable and sticky... but the TRM says 0x1000 DMA_MODE with SWR bit 0.

Possibility 2: **SWR requires the MTL/MAC clocks (clk_tx_i from the PHY or the CRU 125M).** We enabled `clk_gmac0_125m_src` at 125 MHz. But is that actually the *tx* clock reaching the MAC? In the TRM, `clk_gmac0_125m_src` is "the functional clock" — for RGMII with clock_in_out=output, the SoC drives TXC from this clock. Should be fine.

But hold on: **SDGMAC_GRF `gmac0_clk_gating_en` (bit 0)** — "GMAC0 memory clock gate enable, active high". My gm_rgmii_mode writes 0 to it, i.e. clock on. So the DMA SWR is polled **before** gm_rgmii_mode clears the clock gating bit!

The reset default of `gmac0_clk_gating_en` is probably 1 (gated!) or 0. If the memory clock gate is enabled by default (or left enabled by the bootloader), the DMA has no memory clock → SWR never completes. That fits perfectly: the CSR block is clocked (pclk/aclk) so register writes work, but the DMA's memory/interface clock is gated so its internal reset can't finish.

Fix: program SDGMAC_GRF (RGMII mode + ungated memory clock) **before** the DMA software reset.

That's a very plausible and cheap fix. Also the CRU soft reset (aresetn/presetn) might be fine.

Possibility 3: The DMA also needs the MAC's RX/TX clocks; but for SWR only the CSR clock + the "application clock" are needed.

Possibility 4: `MAC_CONFIGURATION.TE/RE` etc. irrelevant.

Possibility 5: Actually, in stmmac's dwmac4_dma_reset, after setting SWR it waits and returns -EBUSY on timeout — same behavior. In Linux dwmac4, `stmmac_reset` (the DMA reset) is called *after* clocks are enabled and after `dwmac4_set_umac_addr`? No: `stmmac_dvr_probe` → `stmmac_hw_init` → ... `stmmac_open` → `stmmac_init_dma_engine`? Actually the sequence in Linux `stmmac_dvr_probe`:
- clk_prepare_enable (stmmac_clk, pclk, tx/rx)
- stmmac_reset() → dwmac4_dma_reset → "DMA reset" with DMA_BUS_MODE_SFT_RESET
- then stmmac_hw_setup...

And for rockchip, `dwmac_rk` uses `stmmac_pltfr` … the important part: Linux enables the 125 MHz `stmmaceth` clock and (for rockchip) sets up the GRF *before* the DMA reset? In `rk_gmac_setup` / `rk_fix_speed_data`, the GRF is programmed at `set_to_rgmii` during `stmmac_hw_setup`/`fix_mac_speed`. Hmm, and rk's `gmac_clk_enable` enables clocks.

But for us, the SDGMAC_GRF memory-clock-gate bit is the suspicious one. Also: the RK3576's `gmac0_clk_gating_en` gates the "memory clock" of the GMAC (the clock to the MAC's internal RAM/FIFO?), and the reset value... Let me check the TRM reset value for that bit! If reset = 1 (gated), then by default the controller is gated, and SWR would hang exactly like this.

Let me look at the TRM for the reset value of `gmac0_clk_gating_en` in SDGMAC_GRF_GMAC0_CON. Earlier I read:
```
gmac0_clk_gating_en
GMAC0 memory clock gate enable, active high.
```

No explicit reset value shown in the scattered text, but the whole field block had rows: I saw "15:12 RO", then various RW fields with 0x0 reset values. Let me dig: the register GMAC0_CON bit fields. Actually, I realize there's a better diagnostic: the log shows NO "SDGMAC_GRF mode 0x.... -> 0x...." line, which means `before == after` for the masked bits — i.e. the register already had RMII=0, TXCLK_SEL=0, CLK_GATING_EN=0, RMII_CLK_GATE=0 when read. 2. wait 10 µs
3. deassert (write 0s)

Hmm. Two candidate causes:

B) The CRU softreset polarity is inverted, leaving the controller (or its DMA) in reset.

How to distinguish? Add logging around the soft reset: read back SOFTRST_CON42 after writing, and check the CRU's own readback. But the hiword-write-enable means reads return the low 16 bits = the current reset state. So I can log `crst before/after` — that tells us whether the bits are set (asserted) or clear at each step, but not the polarity.

Better idea for distinguishing: **try without the soft reset at all** (variant 2), or **do the DMA reset before the CRU reset**. Actually the cleanest: reorder so that the SDGMAC_GRF is programmed first, then reset the DMA; and if the DMA reset still hangs, skip the CRU soft reset (a candidate to isolate).

But "one variable at a time" — the user flashes once per iteration, so I should make ONE change per flash. Which single change is most likely right?

Let me think harder about which is more likely, using the evidence:

Evidence: the register write to DMA_MODE *landed* (SWR read back as 1). So the APB/AXI CSR path is alive → the CRU resets are NOT asserted (else the register file would likely be dead too, and reads would return 0). For a soft-reset of a bus slave, typically the register file is reset too, so reads would give reset values (0). SWR would read 0 → loop exits OK. So B predicts "reset completed", not a hang. Therefore B is unlikely.

Therefore: the block is *out* of reset and its registers work, but the DMA's internal reset doesn't complete. What does SWR need? From the DWC EQOS databook: "DMA_MODE.SWR ... - `clk_tx_i` / `clk_rx_i` (MAC line clocks from clk_gmac<n>_125m_src) — we enabled clk_gmac0_125m_src and read 125 MHz.

Registers work → the domain is on (or the registers are in an always-on part). Hmm, but partially: if PD_SDGMAC is off, would the APB CSR accesses work? The GMAC's APB slave is inside the power domain, so no. So PD_SDGMAC must be on. 

So the fix: reorder — program SDGMAC_GRF (RGMII mode + ungated memory clock + TX clock source) **before** the DMA software reset. That's one coherent change and it's also more correct in general (the GRF config is part of "platform power", not "MAC config").

Hmm, but is it enough? Let me also consider: does the DMA need the PHY's RX clock? In RGMII with `clock_in_out=output`, the SoC drives TXC; the RX clock comes from the PHY (RXC pin). The MAC's `clk_rx_i` is fed from the PHY's RXC via the IO. **If the PHY is not powered/linked, the RX clock may be absent** → the RxDMA could fail to reset! 

Hmm! That's a real concern: on many MACs, the DMA reset needs both clk_tx and clk_rx. In dwmac-rk, `stmmaceth` (the 125M) is the *TX* clock, and the RX clock comes from the PHY's RXC pin... Since the PHY was reset and released before gm_reset (gm_board_power runs before), the PHY should be generating RXC. But before autoneg completes, the PHY's RXC may be 25 MHz or off.

Hmm, Linux's dwmac4_dma_reset is called at probe with the PHY possibly not even reset yet, and it works. So the RX clock likely isn't required (the databook says the DMA reset requires "the clocks to the DMA" = csr + the application clock (aclk); the tx/rx clocks affect the MAC, not the DMA CSR).

OK so the strongest hypothesis remains the memory-clock gate in SDGMAC_GRF.

Wait — actually, let me look at the TRM once more for the GMAC0_CON reset value of bit 0 and check whether there are more gates. Let me read the whole GMAC0_CON field list with bit rows and reset values.

Also, there's another thing in SDGMAC_GRF: `SDGMAC_GRF_MEM_GATE` at 0x0048 and `SDGMAC_GRF_MEM_CON` — "Interface configuration for HDSPRF type memory in PD_SDGMAC" / "PD_SDGMAC memory". If the GMAC's FIFO RAM requires a memory-repair/init sequence (like VEPU's "memory-repair initial reset" mentioned in the VEPU Kconfig), that could be why the DMA reset hangs!

Let me look at SDGMAC_GRF_MEM_CON and MEM_GATE in the TRM. If PD_SDGMAC's memories need a "memory repair" handshake (MEM_CON with a "start" bit), a driver must do it. Hmm, that would be a big deal.

/****************************************************************************
 * IEEE 802.3 clause 22 Ethernet PHY.
 *
 * A PHY is a device on a two-wire bus, and that is all the MAC driver needs
 * to know about it: who is there, how to start autonegotiation, and what was
 * negotiated.  The bus itself -- MDIO, on this SoC inside the MAC -- is the
 * MAC driver's business, so this layer asks for it through three callbacks
 * instead of assuming a register layout.
 *
 * The split is deliberate and both halves are real files:
 *
 *   drivers/drivers/ethernet_phy/   clause 22 itself: presence probing, the
 *                                   address search, advertisement, restarting
 *                                   autonegotiation, and resolving the result
 *                                   (including the 1000BASE-T registers, which
 *                                   are not part of the 10/100 set)
 *   drivers/drivers/mae0621a/       the part: its strap quirks and what it
 *                                   advertises
 *
 * NuttX's own <nuttx/net/mii.h> already names the registers and the BMCR/BMSR
 * bits; this header adds only what clause 22 has and NuttX does not (the
 * gigabit advertisement and status pair) and the interface between the two
 * halves above.
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __INCLUDE_DRIVERS_ETHERNET_PHY_H
#define __INCLUDE_DRIVERS_ETHERNET_PHY_H

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <nuttx/compiler.h>
#include <nuttx/config.h>

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef CONFIG_ETH_PHY_C22

/****************************************************************************
 * Pre-processor Definitions
 ****************************************************************************/

/* The gigabit pair.  Registers 9 and 10 are the 1000BASE-T control and status
 * registers; they are not in NuttX's <nuttx/net/mii.h>, which stops at the
 * 10/100 set.
 */

#define ETH_PHY_CTRL1000   0x09     /* 1000BASE-T control                  */
#define ETH_PHY_STAT1000   0x0a     /* 1000BASE-T status                   */

/* Control (register 9): what we advertise. */

#define ETH_PHY_ADV_1000HALF (1 << 10)
#define ETH_PHY_ADV_1000FULL (1 << 11)

/* Status (register 10): what was agreed.  These are the *negotiated* result
 * bits, not the capability bits in [15:14].
 */

#define ETH_PHY_LPA_1000HALF (1 << 10)
#define ETH_PHY_LPA_1000FULL (1 << 11)

/* The 10/100 advertisement every clause 22 PHY understands: all four modes
 * and the IEEE 802.3 selector field.
 */

#define ETH_PHY_ANAR_10_100 \
  (MII_ADVERTISE_10BASETXHALF | MII_ADVERTISE_10BASETXFULL |               \
   MII_ADVERTISE_100BASETXHALF | MII_ADVERTISE_100BASETXFULL |             \
   MII_ADVERTISE_8023)

/* Address used when no PHY answered. */

#define ETH_PHY_ADDR_NONE  0xff

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Types
 ****************************************************************************/

/* The MDIO bus, as the MAC driver implements it.  `arg` is the MAC's own
 * state; the PHY layer only passes it back.  Both calls run in thread
 * context.
 */

struct eth_phy_bus_s
{
  CODE int (*read)(FAR void *arg, uint8_t phyaddr, uint8_t regaddr,
                   FAR uint16_t *value);
  CODE int (*write)(FAR void *arg, uint8_t phyaddr, uint8_t regaddr,
                    uint16_t value);
  FAR void *arg;
};

/* What one part is like.  Everything here is a property of the silicon or of
 * the board's straps, so it is data, and a new PHY of this kind is a new
 * instance of this structure rather than a new state machine.
 */

struct eth_phy_desc_s
{
  FAR const char *name;

  /* The address the board strapped in.  The search order is this one, then
   * zero if `try_zero`, then a scan of 1..31.
   */

  uint8_t strapaddr;
  bool try_zero;

  /* Some parts answer at two addresses: their strap pins select one, and a
   * "PHY address 0 also valid" strap defaults to enabled, which is why a
   * vendor device tree may say reg = <0> for a PHY strapped to 1.  Probing
   * the strap value first and 0 second covers that without having to know
   * which of the two the device tree named.
   */

  uint16_t anar;                /* 10/100 advertisement                 */
  uint16_t gbcr;                /* 1000BASE-T advertisement             */

  /* A part with no usable PHY ID registers is identified by a present BMSR
   * instead: extended-capability set, and neither all-ones nor all-zeros.
   */

  bool has_id;
};

/* One PHY on one bus.  Opaque to callers; allocated by eth_phy_initialize().
 */

struct eth_phy_s;

/* The result of reading the link. */

struct eth_phy_link_s
{
  bool up;                      /* link is up                           */
  uint16_t speed;               /* 10, 100 or 1000 (Mbit/s)             */
  bool full_duplex;
};

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Function Prototypes
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifdef __cplusplus
#define EXTERN extern "C"
extern "C"
{
#else
#define EXTERN extern
#endif

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: eth_phy_initialize
 *
 * Description:
 *   Find the PHY and take a reference to it.  Nothing is written to the part
 *   except its 10/100 and 1000BASE-T advertisements, which autonegotiation
 *   will use when it is started.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   bus  - how to reach the MDIO bus (the MAC driver owns it)
 *   desc - the part, and the address the board strapped in
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   A handle, or NULL if no PHY answered (the caller decides whether that is
 *   fatal; on this board a missing PHY only means the port cannot be used).
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

FAR struct eth_phy_s *
eth_phy_initialize(FAR const struct eth_phy_bus_s *bus,
                   FAR const struct eth_phy_desc_s *desc);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: eth_phy_uninitialize
 ****************************************************************************/

void eth_phy_uninitialize(FAR struct eth_phy_s *phy);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: eth_phy_addr
 *
 * Description:
 *   The MDIO address the part actually answered at, or ETH_PHY_ADDR_NONE.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

uint8_t eth_phy_addr(FAR struct eth_phy_s *phy);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: eth_phy_name
 ****************************************************************************/

FAR const char *eth_phy_name(FAR struct eth_phy_s *phy);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: eth_phy_start
 *
 * Description:
 *   Advertise what the part can do and restart autonegotiation.  Called when
 *   the interface comes up, which is the first thing that may write to the
 *   part.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int eth_phy_start(FAR struct eth_phy_s *phy);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: eth_phy_link
 *
 * Description:
 *   Read the link state and, once autonegotiation has finished, what was
 *   agreed.
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   OK with `link->up` set or clear; -EAGAIN while the link is up but
 *   autonegotiation has not finished (nothing to report yet); another negated
 *   errno if the part could not be read.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int eth_phy_link(FAR struct eth_phy_s *phy,
                 FAR struct eth_phy_link_s *link);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: eth_phy_read_reg / eth_phy_write_reg
 *
 * Description:
 *   Raw clause 22 access, for the MAC driver's SIOCxMIIREG passthrough.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int eth_phy_read_reg(FAR struct eth_phy_s *phy, uint8_t regaddr,
                     FAR uint16_t *value);
int eth_phy_write_reg(FAR struct eth_phy_s *phy, uint8_t regaddr,
                      uint16_t value);

#undef EXTERN
#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* CONFIG_ETH_PHY_C22 */
#endif /* __INCLUDE_DRIVERS_ETHERNET_PHY_H */

/****************************************************************************
 * Maxio MAE0621A gigabit Ethernet PHY (datasheet: mae0621a-spec.txt).
 *
 * A plain clause 22 part with two quirks that are worth knowing before its
 * address is treated as a constant:
 *
 * 1. **It has no PHY ID.**  The register map (spec 8.2) does not list
 *    registers 2 and 3, so identification is not an option and presence has
 *    to be decided from the status register.  This is what the descriptor's
 *    `has_id = false` says.
 *
 * 2. **It answers at two addresses.**  The board's strap block pulls
 *    PHYAD0 up and PHYAD1/PHYAD2 down, so PHYAD[2:0] = 001 and the part
 *    answers at 1.  But PHYCR1 (page 0xA43, register 24) bit 13, "PHYAD_0
 *    Enable", defaults to set: "a command with PHY address = 0 is valid,
 *    MDC/MDIO will respond".  So address 0 works too, which is why a vendor
 *    device tree can say reg = <0> for a PHY strapped to 1.
 *
 * Its RGMII delays are strap-only (RXD1 = TXDLY, RXD0 = RXDLY, each 2 ns);
 * PHYCR1, PHYCR2 and MIICR contain no delay bits.  That is board wiring, not
 * a driver matter, and it is why the SoC's side of the delay is programmed by
 * the MAC driver rather than negotiated here.
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __INCLUDE_DRIVERS_MAE0621A_H
#define __INCLUDE_DRIVERS_MAE0621A_H

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <nuttx/compiler.h>
#include <nuttx/config.h>

#include <stdint.h>

#include "ethernet_phy.h"

#ifdef CONFIG_ETH_PHY_MAE0621A

/****************************************************************************
 * Pre-processor Definitions
 ****************************************************************************/

/* The address the strap block's own table names as the default: PHYAD[2:0] =
 * 001.  A board that straps differently passes its own value.
 */

#define MAE0621A_STRAP_ADDR 1

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Function Prototypes
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifdef __cplusplus
#define EXTERN extern "C"
extern "C"
{
#else
#define EXTERN extern
#endif

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: mae0621a_initialize
 *
 * Description:
 *   Find and describe a MAE0621A on the given MDIO bus.  Writes nothing to
 *   the part except its advertisements; autonegotiation is started later, by
 *   eth_phy_start(), when the interface comes up.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   bus       - how to reach the MDIO bus (the MAC driver owns it)
 *   strapaddr - the address the board's PHYAD straps select
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   A handle, or NULL if no PHY answered at the strap address, at zero, or
 *   anywhere on the bus.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

FAR struct eth_phy_s *mae0621a_initialize(FAR const struct eth_phy_bus_s *bus,
                                          uint8_t strapaddr);

#undef EXTERN
#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* CONFIG_ETH_PHY_MAE0621A */
#endif /* __INCLUDE_DRIVERS_MAE0621A_H */

/****************************************************************************
 * Maxio MAE0621A gigabit Ethernet PHY.
 *
 * The part is plain clause 22, so all of the state machine is in
 * drivers/drivers/ethernet_phy/ and what is left here is what makes this part
 * different: it has no PHY ID registers, and it answers at address zero as
 * well as at its strapped address.  Both are described to the shared layer as
 * data (drivers/include/ethernet_phy.h) rather than as code, which is the
 * whole reason that layer takes a descriptor.
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <nuttx/config.h>

#include <stdint.h>

#include "ethernet_phy.h"
#include "mae0621a.h"

#ifdef CONFIG_ETH_PHY_MAE0621A

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Data
 ****************************************************************************/

/* What this part advertises.
 *
 * The RGMII delays are strap-only on this part, so nothing here depends on
 * them, and pause frames are deliberately not advertised: the MAC driver does
 * not program the MAC's TX/RX flow control either, and advertising a
 * capability the MAC will not honour is worse than not having it.
 */

static const struct eth_phy_desc_s g_mae0621a_desc =
{
  .name     = "MAE0621A",
  .try_zero = true,             /* PHYAD_0 Enable defaults to set          */
  .anar     = ETH_PHY_ANAR_10_100,
  .gbcr     = ETH_PHY_ADV_1000FULL | ETH_PHY_ADV_1000HALF,
  .has_id   = false,            /* spec 8.2: no registers 2 and 3          */
};

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

FAR struct eth_phy_s *mae0621a_initialize(FAR const struct eth_phy_bus_s *bus,
                                          uint8_t strapaddr)
{
  struct eth_phy_desc_s desc = g_mae0621a_desc;

  /* The descriptor is static because the PHY handle keeps a pointer to it,
   * and only the strap address differs between boards.  A local copy would
   * dangle, so this one is patched through a per-call static descriptor
   * table instead -- see below.
   */

  desc.strapaddr = strapaddr;
  return eth_phy_initialize_private(bus, &desc);
}

#endif /* CONFIG_ETH_PHY_MAE0621A */

	int "Receive descriptor ring depth"
	default 16
	range 4 64
	---help---
		Number of receive descriptors, which is also the receive quota:
		one netpkt is held per slot for as long as the interface is up,
		out of CONFIG_IOB_NBUFFERS.  Each port claims this many, so a
		two-port build holds twice as many.

	int "Transmit descriptor ring depth"
	default 8
	range 4 64

	default n

	default n
	select SPI
	---help---
		Enable the RK3576 SPI master driver (Synopsys DesignWare SSI,

	bool "Watchdog Timer (WDT)"
	default n
	select WATCHDOG
	---help---
		Enable the RK3576 Watchdog Timer lower-half driver (TRM Part1
		Ch15).  A 32-bit down-counter that resets the SoC when it reaches
		zero; the counter is kicked by writing 0x76 to WDT_CRR.

		The SoC exposes six instances (PMU/NPU/DDR/S/NS/BUS).  Of these,
		only WDT_NS (non-secure world, fixed 24 MHz) is usable from NuttX
		and is what rk3576_wdt_initialize() actually implements.  The PMU

	default n

		The PHY contains the TMDS/eDP PLL, the four serialiser lanes and
		the sideband block, and is shared between the HDMI and eDP
		controllers -- the VOP can drive only one of them at a time.

		On the HDMI path it is the PHY, not the CRU, that generates the

	default n

	select VIDEO_FB

	---help---
		Enable the RK3576 Video Output Processor (VOP @ 0x27d00000).

		display interface clocks (dclk_vp0/1/2). dclk_vp0 is the pixel clock

		payload as a parallel pixel stream with sync signals.  It does

		Enable the RK3576 Video Capture controller (VICAP @ 0x27c10000),
		which takes the parallel pixel stream produced by a CSI HOST (or
		the DVP port), filters it by virtual channel and data type, crops
		it, and DMAs it to DDR.

		This driver implements the MIPI input path for image capture and
		registers the result with the NuttX capture framework as
		/dev/videoN, implementing the SoC side of the V4L2 capture
		interface (struct imgdata_s).  An image sensor driver (struct
		imgsensor_s) is required as well; the framework binds at most one
		available sensor per capture device.

		Frames are written with the VICAP MMU bypassed, so the capture
		buffers must be physically contiguous and below 4GB -- hence
		depending on the RK3576 DMA heap allocator.

		The VICAP input has no RAW pixel format in the capture
		framework's format table, so the RAW sensor data is demosaiced on
		the CPU inside this driver and the framework is presented with the
		finished NV12/YUV420 frame.  That keeps the frame buffer written by
		DMA and the buffer handed to the framework separate, and it avoids
		having to extend the shared format tables.

config RK3576_VEPU
	bool "Video Encoder (VEPU510)"
	default n
	---help---
		Enable the RK3576 hardware video encoder (VEPU510 at 0x27a00000),
		which implements H.264/H.265 and JPEG encoding.  Only the H.264
		fixed-QP path is driven so far.

		This provides power-domain, reset and clock bring-up, the
		register layer that programs an encode, the job layer that runs
		one on the hardware, and a V4L2 mem-to-mem device that presents
		the result to applications.

		The probe validates the whole power/clock/reset path in one step by
		reading the VEPU510 version register, which cannot answer until
		PD_VEPU0 is out of its memory-repair initial reset and its register
		bus is clocked -- so a version read is a genuine end-to-end check
		rather than a smoke test.

if RK3576_VEPU

config RK3576_VEPU_SELFTEST
        bool "Encode synthetic pictures at boot"
        default y
        ---help---
                At boot, hand the encoder pictures built in memory and log what
                comes back: the bitstream length, the distortion figure, the
                interrupt status, and how many macroblocks were coded intra.

                This is the acceptance test for the encode path itself, the way the
                version probe is for the clocks and resets. The pictures are
                synthesised rather than captured, so a failure cannot be the
                camera's fault, and the configuration is the plainest one the
                register layer supports, so it cannot be a syntax bug either.

                There are two halves. One encodes a still picture three ways and
                checks the sizes come back in the order their complexity implies.
                The other encodes a moving sequence as one IDR followed by P
                pictures and checks that predicting costs less than not predicting
                -- a failure that is otherwise silent, because a stream whose
                prediction has stopped working still decodes, just at the wrong
                rate. See chips/rk3576/vepu/README.md.

                It costs about a megabyte of the DMA heap for the duration of the
                test, which is released as soon as the result is logged. Turn it off
                once the path is known good.

config RK3576_VEPU_SEQ_DUMP
        bool "Log the sequence test's bitstream in hex at boot"
        default n
        depends on RK3576_VEPU_SELFTEST
        ---help---
                Log the whole of the sequence test's output as hex, one line per 64
                bytes, so it can be read back on a host with a decoder rather than
                from a terminal.

                Off by default: it is a few hundred lines of log for one picture,
                and what it is for is comparing the encoder's own picture against a
                host decoder's, which is a bring-up activity rather than a boot one.

endif # RK3576_VEPU

config RK3576_VEPU_CODEC
        bool "V4L2 memory-to-memory encoder device"
        default n
        depends on RK3576_VEPU
        depends on VIDEO_STREAM
        select SCHED_WORKQUEUE
        select SCHED_HPWORK
        ---help---
                Present the encoder as a /dev/videoN node that takes NV12 frames
                on its output side and returns an H.264 elementary stream on its
                capture side, using the V4L2 mem-to-mem framework.

                The output is annex-B and the stream's first frame carries the
                sequence and picture parameter sets in front of it, so what comes
                out of the device can be written to a file and played directly.

                A job is started by the queue operation that submits it and
                finished by the hardware's interrupt, so the bitstream is waited
                for with poll() on the device rather than by the queue operation
                blocking.  The completion runs on the high-priority work queue.

                This is a fixed-QP encoder. There is no rate control, and the frame
                rate only reaches the bitstream as VUI timing. Pictures are grouped,
                and all but the first of a group predict from the picture before
                them; see RK3576_VEPU_DEFAULT_GOP for the group length and why it is
                what it is.

if RK3576_VEPU_CODEC

config RK3576_VEPU_CODEC_SELFTEST
        bool "Run the encoder through its own V4L2 interface at boot"
        default y
        ---help---
                At boot, open the encoder's device node and drive it the way an
                application has to: negotiate both formats, request and map
                buffers, stream, and check the bitstream that comes back.

                This is the counterpart of RK3576_VEPU_SELFTEST one layer up.
                That one proves the hardware encodes a frame; this one proves an
                application can reach it, which is a different claim. The three
                frames it encodes have different amounts of detail in them, so
                the sizes coming back in the right order is what says the encoder
                is responding to the picture.

### The PHY: NuttX has a descriptor, not a framework

Settled after the first run, by reading the tree rather than deciding in the
abstract. The finding, because it will come up again:

- **No PHY driver layer exists.** No `phy_dev_s`, no `mdio_bus`, no
  `drivers/net/phy/`, no functions in `mii.h` (its prototype section is empty).
  `<nuttx/net/phy.h>` + `drivers/net/phy_notify.c` are the SIGIO link
  notification service and nothing else.
- **A PHY *descriptor* does exist**: `struct phy_desc_s` in
  `include/nuttx/net/mii.h` — name, id1/id2, a vendor `status` register, an
  `address_lo`/`address_high` range, and the `mbps10/100/1000`, `duplex`,
  `speed_mask` fields that decode that register. The board supplies it
  (`BOARD_ENETn_PHY_LIST` in `boards/arm64/imx9/imx93-evk/include/board.h`)
  and the MAC driver walks it (`imx9_determine_phy()`).
- **Every MAC driver carries its own clause 22 code**, and the board supplies a
  `<chip>_phy_boardinitialize(int intf)` hook for reset/power
  (`CONFIG_IMXRT_ENET_PHYINIT` and friends). imxrt additionally keeps a
  `static struct phy_desc_s g_board_phys[]`; mpfs instead blind-scans the bus
  (`mpfs_phyfind()`, `PHYID1 != 0xffff` over 0..31).

So the driver follows NuttX: **clause 22 is inline in `rk3576_gmac.c`**, the
part is the board's `struct phy_desc_s` (`kickpi_k7_ethernet.c`), and the two
pieces of meaning that structure does not spell out are stated where they are
used:

| field | value | means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id1`/`id2` | both 0 | the part has **no PHY ID registers**; identify by status register only (the MAE0621A lists no registers 2 or 3) |
| `status` | `0xffff` | the part has **no vendor status register**; use clause 22's own (BMSR + the 1000BASE-T pair) |
| `address_lo` | 1 | the strap block's PHYAD[2:0] = 001; `address_high = 0xffff` = this one address only |
| `clause` | 22 | clause 45 is rejected with `-ENOTSUP` |

The address search is the descriptor's range first, then the rest of the bus,
because the MAE0621A answers at 0 as well (PHYCR1 "PHYAD_0 Enable" defaults
set) — which is also why the vendor DTB says `reg = <0>` for a PHY strapped
to 1.

**An earlier attempt put clause 22 in `drivers/drivers/` as its own driver**
(`ethernet_phy/` + `mae0621a/`, with a project `ethernet_phy.h`). It was
removed: it duplicated `struct phy_desc_s`, it would have been the only PHY
driver in the tree organised that way, and it made the chip driver depend on
the project driver tree's include path. `drivers/` is back to its original
state.

### First hardware run — what it proved, and what changed because of it

The board reported:

```
gmac0: 125m clock 125000000 Hz
gmac0: DMA software reset never completed
ERROR: GMAC0 initialization failed: -110
```

Three things follow, and all three are now in the code:

1. **The clock tree and the APB path are alive.** The 125 MHz divider reaches
   exactly 125 MHz (open item 2 closed), and the CSR write stuck and read back
   as 1 — so `PD_SDGMAC` is powered, `aclk`/`pclk` are running, and the CRU
   reset polarity reading ("1 asserts") is right. A block held in reset would
   have read 0 and the poll would have passed.
2. **DMA `SWR` needs a clock we do not have yet.** The TRM is explicit: SWR
   "is automatically cleared after the reset operation is complete in all
   DWC_ether_qos clock domains", and "it is essential that all PHY input
   clocks ... are present". In RGMII that includes RXC, which the PHY drives
   and which need not be running before the link has trained. **The driver no
   longer uses SWR**: `gm_reset()` asserts the two per-port CRU bits
   (`aresetn`, `presetn`) and verifies they released, which needs no IP clock.
3. **The GRF is now programmed before the reset**, not after: it is platform
   state, and a controller reset does not touch it.

The aliveness log now reads both sides of the reset on one line —
`gmac0: version 0x00003051 (0x00000000 before reset)` — so the next flash says
whether the block was ever alive, rather than only that it is not now.

## 做了什么

**1. 删掉我上一轮加的那层，`drivers/` 回到原样**

`drivers/drivers/ethernet_phy/`、`drivers/drivers/mae0621a/`、`drivers/include/ethernet_phy.h`、`drivers/include/mae0621a.h` 全部删除，`drivers/drivers/Kconfig` 的两条 `source` 撤回——`git status drivers/` 现在为空。

**2. PHY 逻辑内联回 [rk3576_gmac.c](contest2026_062_PharosTech/chips/rk3576/rk3576_gmac.c)，用 NuttX 的 `struct phy_desc_s`**

- MDIO 读写、存在性判断、地址搜索、广告+重启自协商、链路解析都在驱动器里，和 imx9/imxrt/stm32 一个形状。
- PHY 是**数据**：[kickpi_k7_ethernet.c](contest2026_062_PharosTech/boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/src/kickpi_k7_ethernet.c) 里两个 `static const struct phy_desc_s`，`name/id1/id2/status/address_lo/address_high/clause`。
- 两处 `phy_desc_s` 表达不了的语义，写在用它的地方：
  - `id1 == 0 && id2 == 0` → 这颗 PHY **没有 ID 寄存器**，只按状态寄存器认（MAE0621A 的 8.2 节没有 2、3 号寄存器）；
  - `status == 0xffff` → **没有厂商状态寄存器**，走 clause 22 自己的 BMSR + 1000BASE-T 那对寄存器。
- 链路解析支持两种：`status != 0xffff` 时按描述符的 `speed_mask/mbps*/duplex` 解码（imx9 的做法），否则走 clause 22。以后换一颗有厂商状态寄存器的 PHY，只改板级描述符，不动驱动。
- 地址搜索：先按描述符给的区间（1），再扫全总线（0..31）——因为 MAE0621A 的 `PHYAD_0 Enable` 默认使能，地址 0 也应答，这正是 vendor DTB 敢写 `reg = <0>` 的原因。
- 副作用是好的：`CONFIG_RK3576_GMAC` 不再 `depends on NYABULA_CUSTOM_DRIVERS`，`chips/.../Make.defs` 里那条给 PHY 头文件用的 `-I` 也撤了——芯片驱动不再依赖项目驱动树的 include 路径。

**3. 顺带修了首次上板暴露的那个问题**

`DMA_MODE.SWR` 自清不掉，根因是 TRM 那句话：SWR 要求*所有* clock domain 都在跑，RGMII 下包括 PHY 驱动的 RXC，而链路还没 train 时它可能不跳。所以 `gm_reset()` 现在**只用 CRU 的两个 per-port 复位位**（`aresetn`/`presetn`），置位后读回确认已释放——CRU 复位不需要 IP 时钟。同时把 SDGMAC_GRF 和 VCCIO 的编程移到复位之前（属于 platform 状态，复位不碰它们）。

## 这版日志说明了什么

- `version 0x00003051` **前后都是** → 控制器活着,PD_SDGMAC 已供电、aclk/pclk 在跑、CRU 复位极性判断正确。

- 没有 `SDGMAC_GRF mode` 行 = 那些位本来就是 0,写入前后一致。
- `bmsr 0x7949` 解码:bit0 扩展能力、bit3 支持自协商、bit8 扩展状态、bit11..14 = 10M/100M 全半双工;**bit2 链路 = 0**(还没接线/没 up),bit5 自协商完成 = 0(还没启动)。一切正常。
- **`at address 0`,不是 1。** 驱动先按描述符试地址 1,没应答,扫总线在 0 找到——所以这颗 PHY 只应答 0(和 vendor DTB 的 `reg = <0>` 一致,而 schematic 网名推断的"1"是错的)。扫描救了这一次;稍后我会把描述符的 `address_lo` 改成 0,免得每次开机白读 34 个地址(不影响功能)。

## 现在不用重新编译

`ifup` / `ifconfig` / `ping` 都是运行时命令,当前固件就够测 phase 3 和 5。

**A. 接好网线**(两个口任选一个,gigabit 交换机或直连 PC 都行)。

**B. 拉起接口**
```
nsh> ifup eth0
```
等 2–4 秒(自协商 + 每秒一次的轮询),期望出现:
```
gmac0: link up 1000M full
```
同时 RJ45 的 link LED 应点亮。然后看状态:
```
nsh> ifconfig eth0
```

**C. 板子主动发(测 TX,顺带测 RX 收回应)**
```
nsh> ifconfig eth0 192.168.1.50 netmask 255.255.255.0
nsh> ping 192.168.1.10          # 换成你 PC 的地址
```
或者网络里有 DHCP 服务器:
```
nsh> ifconfig eth0 dhcp
```
ping 有回应就说明 TX 和 RX 双向都通了。

**D. PC 主动发(测非请求收包 + ARP 应答)**
在 PC 上 `ping 192.168.1.50`,并 `arp -a` 看板子的 MAC `02:52:4b:37:76:00` 有没有进表。

**E. 看一眼缓冲池**
```
nsh> mem
```
`ifup eth0` 之后应比之前少 16 个 IOB(RX 环),两个口都 up 就少 32;`iob N free` 数字对不上说明环没按预期建起来。

**F. 换第二个口重复 B–D**(`ifup eth1`、`ifconfig eth1 192.168.1.51`)。两条总线的 PHY 同地址不冲突。

## 失败怎么分流

| 现象 | 指向 | 下一步 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ifup` 后 4 秒没有 `link up` 行,LED 不亮 | 物理层/对端:线、水晶头、交换机口、对端强制速率 | 换线换口;看 PC 网卡是否 link;把 PC 网卡设成 auto |
| `link up 100M full`(千兆交换机上) | 只用了两对线,或 TX 时序 | 先换线;仍如此再调 `TX_DELAY0`(改 Kconfig 重编) |
| `link up 1000M full` 但板子 ping 不通,**PC 侧 tcpdump 看不到板子的 ARP 请求** | TX 路径(DMA 发送/描述符) | 见下方"需要你提供的三样" |
| PC 侧能看到板子的 ARP 请求,**但没有回应到达板子** | RX 路径(环、tail、cache、RXC) | 同上 |
| 能 ping 通但丢包 | RGMII 采样时序(33/32 taps) | 调 taps |

关键点:板子上目前没有收发计数器(`CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS` 没开),所以 **PC 侧的 `tcpdump` 是区分 TX/RX 的唯一手段**。

## 如果失败,请给我这三样

1. 串口全文(`ifup` 之后)。
2. `ifconfig eth0` 的输出。
3. PC 上 `sudo tcpdump -ni <有线网卡> -e arp or icmp` 在板子 ping 时的输出。

有这三样我能直接判断是 TX 没出去、还是 RX 没进来,而不必猜。

## 两项已记下的待办(不影响现在的测试)

- 描述符 `address_lo` 改成 0(实测地址),把开机时的 34 次 MDIO 读取减到 1 次。
- 若数据面需要排查,再考虑开 `CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS`(给 `ifconfig` 加收发计数)或加一次性中断日志——按"一次一个变量"的原则,留到确实需要时再加。

The MAE0621A supports auto-negotiation in compliance with IEEE 802.3 clause 28, 40 and IEEE 802.3az. Auto-
negotiation is used to negotiate speed/duplex/flow control and MASTER/SLAVE mode for 1000BASE-T over
UTP twisted pair cable. It performs auto-negotiation priority resolution, pause/asymmetric pause resolution,
and/or 1000BASE-T MASTER/SLAVE resolution based on the information exchanged between the local and
remote devices to determine the best possible operating mode. Auto-negotiation can also advertise the
capability of crossover MDI/MDI-X and EEE power saving between the local device and its link partner.

Auto-negotiation and auto MDI/MDI-X can be enabled and disabled independently. Auto-negotiation can be

## 先说明你这轮测试的结论

- `ifup eth0` / `ifup eth1` 都返回 OK → 驱动起来了、环建好了、自协商已重启。

- 两个 PHY 对连**不依赖 SoC**:它们各用自己的 25M 晶振,千兆下 MDI/MDIX 是自动的(手册 7.6,auto crossover 默认开)。所以"连不上"只可能出在 PHY 侧或我们写 PHY 的方式上。

## 这行怎么读(也方便你自己先判断)

| 字段 | 正常值 | 异常含义 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bmcr` | `0x1100`(ANENABLE=1,RESTART 已自清) | 若读到 `0x1140` 之类 ANENABLE=0 → 我们的写没落到 PHY;若 bit11/bit14 置位 → 被 power-down/loopback |
| `bmsr` bit2 | 置位=有链路 | 一直 0 = 没检测到对端 |
| `bmsr` bit5 | 置位=自协商完成 | 一直 0 = 在对连但协商没走完 |
| `anar` | `0x01e1` | 不是这个值 → 写没落地 |
| `lpa` | 非 0 = **听到了对端** | `0x0000` = 链路伙伴什么都没发过来(线/交叉/对端) |
| `stat1000` | 有 bit10/11 = 千兆协商成功 | 0 = 没到千兆 |

三种典型诊断:
- `lpa 0x0000` + `bmsr` bit2=0 → 对端没被听见:线序/交叉没成,或对端 PHY 没在发。这时**换一根交叉线**或换线材是最快的验证。
- `lpa 0x01e1` 但 bit5 不置位 → 双方在说话但协商没收敛(千兆主从或广告不匹配)。
- `bmcr` 不是 `0x1100` → 我们的写根本没进 PHY(地址 0 只读?),那就是驱动侧问题,我改。

如果最终证明两个 PHY 直连这条路走不通(没有交换机确实可能踩到 MDIX 的坑),还有一个**不需要任何线**的数据面验证办法:让 PHY 进 loopback(BMCR bit14),它会把 TX 直接环回 RX,不需要链路。那需要给驱动加一条受控的测试路径(或者一个 Kconfig 选项),等这次结果出来再决定要不要加——按"一次一个变量"的原则先不动。
补充一下：没有看到网口的led灯点亮

那条 LED 信息很弱,先别当证据用:

MAE0621A 的 **LED0/LED1/LED2 与 CFG_EXT、CFG_LDO[1:0] 是同一组引脚**(手册 7.10)。这三个脚在复位时被采样来决定 RGMII IO 的供电方式,所以板厂要是用它们做 strap,就根本没有 LED 驱动;而且就算当 LED 用,极性也取决于 strap 电平(拉高=低有效,拉低=高有效)。所以"灯不亮"既可能是无链路、也可能是这板子压根没把 LED 接出来。要判定得看原理图那三个脚接了什么,记忆里没有这一条。

双口对连是**最严格**的测试(同时要求两个口都正常 + Auto-MDIX 成功)。如果你手边有任何带以太网口的东西——路由器、笔记本、机顶盒、甚至电视——把 **eth0 接它**,再跑一次 `ifup eth0`:

So even if our writes were ignored, autoneg would run with defaults (ANAR=0x01E1, GBCR=0x0300 typically) → link with the partner PHY at 1000M.

Unless the PHY *doesn't* auto-start autoneg after reset... The datasheet says "Auto-negotiation process will be triggered automatically whenever any one of the following occurs: Power-up, Hardware reset, Software reset, Restart auto-negotiation, Change from power down to power up, Copper link goes down". 失败反而暴露了一个真问题,而且让我上一轮的一个结论站不住了——先纠正:

**"PHY 只应答地址 0、不应答 1"这个结论是我推过头了。** 两次运行的差别只有"先试哪个地址",而两次都是**先试的那个失败**:

| 运行 | 先试 | 结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 第一次(`address_lo=1`) | 1(第一条 MDIO 事务,**失败**) | 扫描试 0 → 成功,记为"地址 0" |
| 这次(`address_lo=0`) | 0(第一条事务,**失败**) | 扫描把 0 当"已试过"跳过 → 1..31 全失败 → `ifup` 报没应答 |

这次测的是**已知正常**的设备(示波器的网口),结果仍然 `lpa 0x0000`——所以不是双口对称的问题,是我们这侧的 PHY 在铜缆上根本不通。手册里有两个寄存器正对着这个症状,而且都只能在厂商页读:

- **PHYSR(页 `0xA43`,地址 `0x1A`)**:bit2 实时链路、bit1 **实际 MDI/MDIX 状态**、bit14 **ALDPS 状态**(1 = PHY 认为"没插网线",3 秒后反映)、bit12 自协商使能、bit5:4 速率。
- **PHYCR1(页 `0xA43`,地址 `0x18`)**:bit2 ALDPS 使能、bit1 **ALDPS 下关 PLL**。这条很可疑:这块板子的 `RXD2` strap 是 `PLLOFF=1`,如果 ALDPS 真的开着,PLL 被关掉后 PHY 就再也发不出也收不到 FLP——表现正好是"MDIO 一切正常、铜缆一声不响"。

页选择寄存器是 **PAGSR = 31(0x1F)**,写完要切回 0。我加一个受 Kconfig 控制的厂商页 dump。
