Excellent, now I have exactly what's needed:

**PHYSR (Page 0xA43, Address 0x1A)**:
- bit 14: ALDPS State (1 = entered link-down power saving, i.e. cable not plugged in, after 3 s)
- bit 12: Auto-Negotiation Enable
- bit 11: Master mode
- bit 5:4 Speed (10 = 1000M, 01 = 100M, 00 = 10M)
- bit 3: Duplex
- bit 2: Link (Real Time)
- bit 1: MDI Crossover Status (1 = MDIX, 0 = MDI)
- bit 0: Jabber (Real Time)

**This is the perfect diagnostic**: it reports the *real-time* link and the *actual MDI/MDIX state*. So:
- If `MDI Crossover Status` = 0 (MDI) and link = 0 forever → the crossover never happened → could be the symmetric-lockstep issue.
- ALDPS State bit tells whether the PHY thinks the cable is unplugged.
- Jabber etc.

**PAGSR = register 31 (0x1F)**, write the page (e.g. 0xA43), access the register, then restore to 0 (or 0xA42).

Also **LCR (Page 0xD04, Address 0x10) = LED Control Register** — the LEDs are configurable and could be disabled! That would explain the dark LEDs. Worth dumping too.

Also PHYCR1 (page 0xA43 reg 0x18) bits: 13 PHYAD0_en, 9 MDI manual, 8 MDI mode, 6 PHYAD non-zero detect, 4 preamble check, 3 jabber, 2 ALDPS enable, 1 ALDPS PLL off.

So now I can add a **one-shot vendor-page dump** at ifup that prints:
- PHYCR1 (0x18): 16 bits
- PHYCR2 (0x19)
- PHYSR (0x1A): the key one
- LCR (page 0xD04 reg 0x10): LED config

And it must switch pages: write reg 0x1F = page, read reg, restore 0x1F = 0.

Careful with page switching: after switching to page 0xA43, registers 0..15 are no longer the standard ones. Our `gm_mdio_read(priv, addr, reg, &val)` just reads a register — fine, page is transparent.

Design: add
```c
static int gm_phy_page_read(priv, uint16_t page, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *val)
{
  int ret = gm_mdio_write(priv, priv->phyaddr, 0x1f, page);
  if (ret < 0) return ret;
  ret = gm_mdio_read(priv, priv->phyaddr, reg, val);
  gm_mdio_write(priv, priv->phyaddr, 0x1f, 0);   /* back to standard registers */
  return ret;
}
```
Note the datasheet: "To access the IEEE Standard Registers 0 to 15, PAGSR should be set to 0 or 0xA42 (default)". So restoring to 0 is fine.

1: # RK3576 GMAC bring-up — two RGMII ports on the KICKPI-K7
2: 
3: The plan for the wired Ethernet of the KICKPI-K7, and every board and register
4: fact it rests on. Written before any of it was implemented, so that the facts
5: do not have to be dug out twice. Replaces nothing; the `beacon` reference
6: driver is deliberately **not** the blueprint — see below.
7: 
8: ## The link
9: 
10: ```
11: RK3576 GMAC0 (0x2A220000, DWC EQOS @ RGMII) ── MAE0621A ── RJ45
12: RK3576 GMAC1 (0x2A230000, DWC EQOS @ RGMII) ── MAE0621A ── RJ45
13: ```
14: 
15: Each controller has its **own MDIO bus**, so the two PHYs may share an MDIO
16: address — and they do (see the PHY section). Nothing about the two ports is
17: shared except the CRU gate register and the clock tree.
18: 
19: ## Do not use the `beacon` driver as a blueprint
20: 
21: `beacon/rk3576-ultimate-bsp:chips/rk3576/rk3576_gmac.c` is a 2035-line driver
22: that is already instance-parameterised (`intf`, `g_rk3576_gmac[2]`) and reads
23: plausibly. It is not an implementation, it is a proposal:
24: 
25: - **It was never compiled and never ran.** Nothing in the tree calls
26:   `rk3576_gmac_initialize()`, no board file implements the PHY reset hook, and
27:   no defconfig ever enabled `CONFIG_RK3576_GMAC`.
28: - **Three verified register errors** (all checked against the TRM; see the
29:   register tables below):
30:   1. It gates the GMAC clocks at `CRU_GATE_CON(32)` (0x0880), which is the NPU
31:      block. The GMAC gates are at `CRU_GATE_CON42` (0x08A8).
32:   2. It programs the RGMII delay lines at `0x26040000 + 0x20 + 4n`. They are in
33:      **VCCIO_IOC** (0x26046000) at `+0x0408..+0x0414`.
34:   3. It models a "`GRF_CLK_CON1` @0x0070, gmac1 shifted by 8". No such register
35:      exists in SDGMAC_GRF; the TX clock divider/source is inside
36:      `SDGMAC_GRF_GMACn_CON` bits [7:3].
37: - Its own comments admit the CRU bits are inferred and "must be checked against
38:   the TRM"; several drivers in that BSP claim the *same* gate bits, so at most
39:   one claimant can be right.
40: 
41: **What it did get right** — and this is worth knowing, because it shows the
42: failure was localised: its *board* constants (`GPIO2_B5`/`GPIO3_A3`, tx_delay
43: `0x21`/`0x20`, `rgmii-rxid`) match the vendor DTB exactly. Its author read the
44: DTS correctly and then guessed the register programming.
45: 
46: ## Board facts — from the vendor DTB, not from inference
47: 
48: Source: the vendor Debian image in the workspace root,
49: `update-rk3576-kickpi-k7-linux-debian-multi-20251209-185038.img`. All twelve
50: DTBs inside it report `model = "Rockchip RK3576 KICKPI K7 Board"` and agree on
51: every value below. Extraction recipe at the end of this file; the carved DTS
52: files are kept in `out/k7dtb/`.
53: 
54: | Item | gmac0 | gmac1 |
55: | --- | --- | --- |
56: | Base | `0x2A220000` | `0x2A230000` |
57: | macirq | SPI 0x125 → **INTID 325** | SPI 0x12d → **INTID 333** |
58: | `phy-mode` | `rgmii-rxid` | `rgmii-rxid` |
59: | `clock_in_out` | `output` (SoC drives TXC) | `output` |
60: | `tx_delay` | `0x21` = **33 taps** | `0x20` = **32 taps** |
61: | `rx_delay` | absent → SoC RX delay off | absent |
62: | Pin group | **`eth0m0`** — GPIO bank 3, IOMUX **af 3** | **`eth1m0`** — GPIO bank 2, IOMUX **af 2** |

		interface (struct imgdata_s).  An image sensor driver (struct
		imgsensor_s) is required as well; the framework binds at most one
		available sensor per capture device.

		Frames are written with the VICAP MMU bypassed, so the capture
		buffers must be physically contiguous and below 4GB -- hence
		depending on the RK3576 DMA heap allocator.

		framework's format table, so the RAW sensor data is demosaiced on
		the CPU inside this driver and the framework is presented with the
		finished NV12/YUV420 frame.  That keeps the frame buffer written by
		DMA and the buffer handed to the framework separate, and it avoids
		having to extend the shared format tables.

## 请这样做

1. 烧新固件。
2. 把 **eth1 接到示波器**(保持已知正常的那台设备)。
3. 运行 `ifup eth1`,等 15 秒。
4. 把**两行 `gmac1:` 输出**(t≈0 和 t≈5s 各一组,共 4 行)发我。

## 同时请换一根网线再试一次

两次失败(双口对连、接示波器)**唯一的共同点是网线**。如果两次用的是同一根,它本身就是嫌疑对象。换一根确认能上网的线,重跑一次 `ifup eth1`,看是否会打出 `link up`。

## 我会从这两行里读什么

| 字段 | 期望(全默认) | 异常含义 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `phycr1` | `0x2018`(bit13 PHYAD_0使能、bit4 前导检测、bit3 jabber) | **bit2=1 → ALDPS 开着**;若同时 bit1=1(这块板 RXD2 strap 就是 PLLOFF),PLL 在链路断开时被关掉,PHY 既发不出也收不到 FLP —— 这与"MDIO 全好、铜缆全哑"完全吻合,修法是清掉这两位 |
| `phycr2` | `0x0023`(bit1 RXC 输出使能、bit0 CLKOUT 使能、bit5 保留为 1) | **bit1=0 → RXC 不输出**,MAC 拿不到接收时钟(虽然不影响铜缆建链,但会挡住后续数据) |
| `physr` | bit12(自协商使能)=1,其余看实况 | **bit2 实时链路**、**bit1 实际 MDI/MDIX**(0=MDI,1=MDIX)、**bit14 ALDPS 状态**(1=PHY 认为没插线)、bit5:4 速率、bit3 双工。两次 dump 之间 bit1 是否变化,能看出交叉重试有没有发生 |
| `lcr` | `0x6251` | LED 模式;默认就是"有链路才亮",所以灯不亮只是印证了无链路,不是新线索 |

另外记一笔:`PHYCR1` bit13 `PHYAD_0 Enable` **默认确实是 1**,所以这颗 PHY 应答地址 0 是设计使然,不是板子 strap 异常——这一点也顺带确认了。

ifup eth1...OK
nsh> gmac1: phy addr 0 bmcr 0x1000 bmsr 0x7949 anar 0x01e1 lpa 0x0000 stat1000 0x0000

现在这组数据非常有价值——它**否掉了我们两个主要猜测**,并且把范围缩到很窄。

## 解码

**`phycr1 = 0x2118`** = bit13(PHYAD_0 使能,默认 1) + bit8(MDI 模式位,默认 1,但 bit9=0 时无效) + bit4(前导检测,默认 1) + bit3(jabber,默认 1) —— **完全是手册默认值**:bit2 ALDPS 使能 = 0、bit1 ALDPS 关 PLL = 0、bit9 手动 MDI = 0(自动交叉开着)。

**`phycr2 = 0x0823`** = bit11(CLKOUT 选 125 MHz)+ bit5(保留默认 1)+ bit1(RXC 输出使能)+ bit0(CLKOUT 使能)。

**`physr = 0x1000`** = 只有 bit12(自协商使能)=1。关键位全 0:bit2 实时链路=0、**bit1 实际 MDI 状态=0(仍是 MDI)**、bit14 ALDPS 状态=0。

**`lcr = 0x6251`** = 手册默认:LED0=10M链路+活动、LED1=100M、LED2=1000M。**所以灯不亮就是"没有链路"**——LED 配置本身是好的。

## 结论

PHY 的配置**没有任何问题**:没掉电、没隔离、没进省电、自协商开、自动交叉开、RXC 输出开、LED 正常。它就是**听不到任何东西**,而且 **5 秒后仍停在 MDI、没有切到 MDIX**——说明连"自动交叉"的状态机都没有推进。

剩下两个候选:

1. **线/配对**:两次失败唯一的共同点就是那根线。
2. **PHY 的铜缆侧根本没在跑**(参考时钟或模拟侧),这时 MDIO 依然完美,但发不出也收不到 FLP——与"自动交叉也不推进"吻合。

## 你有示波器,这两项能一次定死

**a) 先换一根确认能上网的网线**,重跑 `ifup eth1`(不用重烧)。这是最便宜的排除。

**b) 量 PHY 的 CLKOUT(引脚 35)**:`phycr2` 明确写着 CLKOUT 使能且选 125 MHz,所以那里应该有一个 125 MHz 的时钟。**如果这里没有时钟,就是 25M 晶振/PLL 没起来**,后面所有现象都能解释,而且不需要再改驱动。

**c) 量网线的 1/2 脚(发送对)** 在自协商期间:应该能看到约每 16 ms 一次的 10BASE-T 链路脉冲(FLP)。有脉冲=我们的 PHY 在发,问题在配对;完全没脉冲=发送侧没工作。

如果配对是问题,把本侧**强制成 MDIX** 就能连上(MDI↔MDIX 是标准配对;交换机口是 MDIX、PC/示波器这类端点通常是 MDI)。这也顺便检验"自动交叉为何不推进"。我把它做成板级 Kconfig 选项,而不是散在代码里。

## 为什么这么设

直通线要求**一端 MDI、一端 MDIX**。而你这块板测过的两个对端——另一个本板口、示波器的网口——**都是端点设备,按惯例都是 MDI**。也就是说:

- 板(MDI)↔ 板(MDI):错配对,不通;
- 板(MDI)↔ 示波器(MDI):错配对,不通。

**两次测试都需要交叉,而我们的 PHY 自动交叉又没推进(`physr` bit1 一直是 0),所以两次都不可能通**——这和 PHY 好坏无关。生产拓扑是"板接交换机",交换机口是 MDIX,我们作 MDI 恰好正确,所以真实部署可能一直是好的。

## 请这样测(一次固件覆盖两种拓扑)

烧入后:

**实验 1:两口对连(用直通线)**
```
nsh> ifup eth0
nsh> ifup eth1
# 等 15 秒
```
期望:
```
gmac0: PHY MDI forced to MDIX (phycr1 0x....)
gmac0: link up 1000M full
gmac1: PHY MDI forced to MDI (phycr1 0x....)
gmac1: link up 1000M full
```
如果两个口都 link up,立刻可以做数据面测试:
```
nsh> ifconfig eth0 192.168.1.50 netmask 255.255.255.0
nsh> ifconfig eth1 192.168.1.51 netmask 255.255.255.0
nsh> ping 192.168.1.51
```
这一条 ping 会完整穿过"MAC0 → PHY0 → 铜缆 → PHY1 → MAC1",是整条链路最干净的验证。

**实验 2:示波器接 eth0**(eth0 是 MDIX,示波器是 MDI,配对正确)
```
nsh> ifdown eth1
nsh> ifup eth0
# 等 15 秒,看有没有 link up
```

与时钟有关的可写位只有这些,全都不是"开晶振":

**没有任何寄存器选择"晶振 vs 外部时钟",也没有 PLL 使能位。** 手册 6.3 写得很清楚:pin 36 = XTAL_IN,pin 37 = XTAL_OUT/EXT_CLK;用晶振就接晶振,**用外部 25M 就把 XTAL_IN 接地、把时钟从 pin 37 灌进去**。这是纯硬件选择,软件无法开关。

## 而且可以确定 PHY 不在复位里

强证据:我们写进 PHYCR1 的值(`0x2218`/`0x2318`)**在软件复位之后依然保持,并且能读回**。被 PHYRSTB 按住的芯片不可能保留寄存器写入。所以 pin 12 复位是释放的、芯片是活的、供电的——晶振理应工作。

## 那"两端 0 V"怎么解释

很可能是**探头把振荡器压停了**:XTAL_IN 是高阻节点(只有一个 ~1 MΩ 的偏置电阻),10x 无源探头是 10 MΩ 对地,**一接上去直流偏置就被拉到原来的 1/10 左右**,原本 0.6~1 V 的偏置立刻显示成几十毫伏,看起来像 0 V;再叠加 15 pF 的负载电容,25 MHz 振荡常常直接停振。所以这次测量**不能证明晶振没工作**。

更可靠的量法(避开 pin 35 太密的问题):

- **AC 耦合**看 XTAL_OUT(pin 37):起振时通常能看到 0.3~1 Vpp、25 MHz 的正弦/准方波。即使探头让它频偏,AC 耦合下也不该是"完全一条直线"。
- 或者直接用**视觉检查**:晶振本体和两颗负载电容是否贴装(有些板贴的是 DNP);XTAL_IN 是否被直接接地(那就说明设计想用外部时钟)。
- 这三种情况指向的结论完全不同:
  - 晶振+电容都在,AC 耦合有波形 → 时钟正常,问题在别处;
  - 晶振没贴 / XTAL_IN 接地 且 EXT_CLK 悬空 → **这块板根本没有给 PHY 提供参考时钟**,是硬件/贴片问题,软件无解。

两个假设现在可以并排检验了,Debian 侧的数据能直接定位:

- **假设 A**:我们的 SoC 没有把 125M TXC 送到 PHY(引脚 20 是输入),而这颗 PHY 在收不到 TXC 时会把链路按住。
- **假设 B**:Linux 给 PHY 绑了专用驱动,写了一些我们没写的厂商寄存器。

## 请在 Debian 下执行这些(按价值排序)

**1. 厂商对 SDGMAC_GRF 和 VCCIO 的编程值(最关键,我手上有我们的值可以逐位对比)**

需要 root:
```sh
devmem 0x26038020 32     # GMAC0_CON
devmem 0x26038024 32     # GMAC1_CON
devmem 0x260460408 32    # VCCIO IOC MISC_CON2 (GMAC0 延时)
devmem 0x260460410 32    # VCCIO IOC MISC_CON4 (GMAC1 延时)
```
(没有 `devmem` 就试 `busybox devmem`;都没有也告诉我。)

**2. 时钟树实际状态(root)**
```sh
cat /sys/kernel/debug/clk/clk_summary | grep -iE "gmac|refclk|25m"
```
我要看 `clk_gmac*_125m_src` 的 rate、`refclko25m_gmac*_out` 是否 enabled。

**3. PHY 是谁、绑了什么驱动**
```sh
ls -l /sys/class/mdio_bus/
for d in /sys/class/mdio_bus/*/*; do echo "$d phy_id=$(cat $d/phy_id) driver=$(basename $(readlink -f $d/driver 2>/dev/null))"; done
```

**4. 链路状态与速率**
```sh
ethtool eth0; ethtool eth1
cat /sys/class/net/eth0/speed /sys/class/net/eth0/carrier
```

**5. 内核日志**
```sh
dmesg | grep -iE "stmmac|gmac|phy|mdio|eth0|eth1|rgmii"
```

**6. MAC 寄存器快照(可与我们的对比)**
```sh
ethtool -d eth0 | head -60
```
重点看 `MAC_CONFIGURATION` 的 **FES(bit14,1=1000M)** 和 **DM(bit13)**——如果厂商是 1000M 而我们这边停在 100M,那 RGMII 时钟就会是 25M 而不是 125M,这本身就能解释 PHY 不建链。

**7. 数据面是否真通**:两个口对连着的情况下,
```sh
ip addr add 192.168.1.50/24 dev eth0
ip addr add 192.168.1.51/24 dev eth1
ping -c3 192.168.1.51
```

- 用第 1 项和我驱动写进去的值(记忆里记着:`GMACn_CON` = txclk_select=CRU + 125M,`VCCIO` = `0x00a1`/`0x00a0`,即 tx_ena + 33/32 taps)逐位对齐;

- 用第 2 项确认 TXC 那条路的时钟到底是谁在供、速率多少;
- 用第 3/4/5 项确认 PHY 是否走了专用驱动(若是,我去读它的 init 序列,把缺的寄存器写进我们的驱动)。

只要其中任一项和我们的值不同,基本就能锁定原因。如果全部一致,那差异就在时序/复位顺序上,我会拿 Debian 的 `dmesg` 时间线(复位→探测→自协商)逐步骤对齐我们的 `ifup` 流程。

text:
Debian 的数据把范围压缩到一个**我们自己的 bug**,而且已修。新固件 mtime **00:19**。

## 从你这轮数据得到的三条更正

| 我们之前的结论 | Debian 显示的事实 |
| --- | --- |
| "MAE0621A 没有 ID 寄存器" | `phy_id = 0x7b744411`,两个口都有。手册寄存器表漏列了 2/3 号 |
| "PHY 在地址 0 应答,地址 1 未验证" | Linux 在 `stmmac-0:00` 找到它——**地址 0 确认** |
| "PHY 的交叉检测不推进" | 同一根直连线下 Linux 能建链,说明它工作正常 |

另外 `refclko25m_gmac*_out` 在 Linux 里确实 enabled(25 MHz),但 GMAC 节点的 pinctrl 没引用 `eth_clk*_25m` 组,所以没到引脚——这个"使能"是装饰性的,可以忽略。我们的 `GMACn_CON` 写入也都是 no-op(寄存器本来就已经是 RGMII/CRU/125M/未门控),**SoC 侧和 Linux 一致**。

## 找到的差异:千兆广告位写错了

```c
#define GM_PHY_ADV_1000FULL (1 << 11)   /* 错!reg 9 的 bit11 是 AS_MASTER */
```

寄存器 9 的正确布局是 **bit9 = 1000BASE-T 全双工、bit10 = 半双工、bit11/12 = 主从手动配置**,而寄存器 10(状态)才是 bit11/10。因此我们写进去的 `0x0c00` 实际含义是:**千兆半双工 + AS_MASTER,完全没有千兆全双工**。而这颗 PHY 自己的 `GBESR` 说它**不支持千兆半双工**——等于我们在千兆上广告了一个自己都进不去的模式。Linux 从 GBESR 推导后写的是 `0x0200`。

已改为 bit9,只广告全双工;两个描述符的 ID 也改成实测的 `0x7b74/0x4410`。

## 这次还加了三个判定寄存器

trace 现在多打一行:

```
gmac0: aner 0x---- ctrl1000 0x---- insr 0x----
```

- **ANER(0x06)**:bit0 = 并行检测故障,bit1 = 链路伙伴支持自协商,bit2 = 收到链路码字;`0x0000` 就意味着**根本没人应答**;
- **ctrl1000(0x09)**:确认我们现在广告的是 `0x0200`;
- **INSR(页 0xA43/0x1D)**:bit3 = 自协商完成,bit0 = 自协商错误。

## 请这样测新固件

1. 烧 **00:19** 的 `nuttx.bin`(这次记一下时间戳,避免再烧到旧的)。
2. 用直通线把两个口连起来。
3. 
```
nsh> ifup eth0
nsh> ifup eth1
# 等 15 秒
```
4. 把 **开机那几行**(现在会带 `id 0x7b744411`)和 `ifup` 之后的输出都发我。

判据很直接:
- 出现 `link up 1000M full` → 就是这个广告位 bug,链路通了立刻 `ifconfig` + `ping` 验证数据面;
- 仍无链路,但 `aner` 非 0、`insr` bit3 置位 → 自协商其实完成了但模式没谈成,看 `lpa`/`stat1000` 的实际值;
- `aner = 0x0000` 且 `insr` 全 0 → PHY 连 FLP 都没收到,那才轮到 TXC/时序,我会接着查;不过有 Debian 的对照,我对这次比较乐观。

cam: wait for the frame worker before its buffers go

The demosaicer runs on the low-priority work queue, and it takes the RAW
buffer it reads and the framework's buffer it writes at the top of a frame
and keeps both for the whole pass.  The epoch check at its end stops a frame
from a stopped stream being delivered, and that check has been read as if it
covered the worker's whole exposure.  It does not: it comes after every read
and write the frame made, so any path that releases or replaces either
buffer while a worker is still demosaicing hands that worker memory which
has already gone back to a heap.

Three paths do exactly that and none of them waited.  The framework frees
the capture frame heap from its close and REQBUFS paths, and that heap is
where the demosaicer's destination lives.  reconfigure frees the RAW buffers
and the demosaic copy, and re-points the geometry the worker reads per
frame.  The driver's own take-down frees the same pair.  The framework's
state for a stopped stream is safe by the time those run -- the epoch check
sees to that -- so what was left open is the buffers.

All three now wait for the worker through work_cancel_sync(): a worker that
is queued but has not started is dropped, and one already running is waited
for.  It sleeps, so it may only be reached where the caller is allowed to
block, which is why the wait is not in stop_capture() -- the framework
reaches that one from the completion callback, with a spinlock held and
preemption disabled.  In reconfigure the wait sits after the input is off
and before the first buffer is touched, so the new geometry is not published
under a worker still reading the old one.

Two pieces of the same state were wrong for more than one CPU, which matters
because the driver is meant to keep working with SMP enabled.  The interrupt
touched the frame state without a lock and relied on this CPU's interrupts
being disabled, which excludes the worker only while there is one CPU; it
takes the worker's lock now, before it reads INTSTAT -- write-one-to-clear,
so two CPUs reading the same pending bits would both act on one frame
boundary.  It also schedules no worker while capturing is false, so a
boundary handled late on another CPU cannot queue one behind a stop that has
already cleared the buffers.  up_disable_irq() stops the interrupt being
delivered, not one already executing elsewhere, and that is what made such a
boundary possible.

None of this changes anything on a single CPU: the worker's and the stop
paths' critical sections already mask this CPU's interrupts, so the
interrupt never contends the lock it now takes.

net: add the RK3576 GMAC driver and the branch's ethernet config

The two on-board ports of the KICKPI-K7 are GMAC0 and GMAC1 of the
RK3576's DWC EQOS ("dwmac-4.20a"), wired RGMII to a Maxio MAE0621A each,
with the PHY reset on a GPIO and the RGMII delays in the VCCIO IOC's
delay lines.  Nothing in the tree drove them, so this adds the driver,
the board layer that describes the two ports, and the configuration the
branch's camera work now shares.

The driver is a netdev lower half: the rings are the quota, one packet
per descriptor, and every descriptor occupies its own cache line so that
one clean or invalidate never touches a neighbour.  The MAC does not
snoop, so the data path does its own maintenance -- clean before handing
a buffer to the DMA, invalidate before reading one back -- and the arch's
range helpers handle the unaligned ends of IOB buffers, which matters
because the RX descriptor points straight at the packet's data area.

Two departures from the plan that came out of reading the TRM rather
than the first run: the DMA's software reset is not used at all.  It
needs every clock domain live, including the PHY's RXC, and RXC may not
be running before the link has trained -- waiting for a bit that cannot
clear cost the first bring-up run a timeout.  The CRU's per-port reset is
stronger and clock-independent, and it is what runs now.  The SDGMAC_GRF
and the IOC delay lines are programmed before that reset, since they are
platform state that a controller reset does not touch.

The PHY follows NuttX rather than inventing a layer: there is no PHY
framework in the tree, so clause 22 lives in the driver, and the board
describes its part with the `struct phy_desc_s` that `mii.h` already
defines -- the same shape imx9 and imxrt use.  The part answers at
address 0 and reports id 0x7b744411; the descriptor carries both, and the
probe still walks the bus when the expected address does not answer,
because the first management transaction after a PHY reset can fail (the
first run's "PHY at 1, then at 0" was that, not a strap).

The link is not up yet, and the one difference found so far against the
vendor kernel was ours: the gigabit advertisement wrote 1 << 11 into
register 9, which is the master/slave bit, so the line advertised
1000BASE-T half duplex (a mode this part cannot enter) and no 1000BASE-T
full duplex at all.  That is corrected here along with the trace that
says where autonegotiation stopped.  What is known to work: the
controller reads its version, the clock tree reaches 125 MHz exactly, and
both PHYs identify themselves.  What does not: nothing trains a link,
while the vendor image on the same board, cable and ports links at once
and pings -- so the remaining fault is in this driver or its board
description, not in the hardware.
MSG

## 方法 2:`dd` + `od`(不需要任何工具)

```sh
dd if=/dev/mem bs=4 skip=$((0x26038020/4)) count=1 2>&1 | od -An -tx4
```
`od -tx4` 直接给 32 位值。若报 `Permission denied`/`Operation not permitted`,说明内核限制了 `/dev/mem`。

## 方法 3:`python3` + mmap(最适合以后写脚本)

```sh
python3 - <<'EOF'
import mmap,os,struct
def rd(a):
    p=a&~0xfff; f=os.open('/dev/mem',os.O_RDONLY|os.O_SYNC)
    m=mmap.mmap(f,0x1000,mmap.MAP_SHARED,mmap.PROT_READ,offset=p)
    v=struct.unpack('<I',m[a-p:a-p+4])[0]; m.close(); os.close(f); return v
for a in (0x26038020,0x26038024,0x260460408,0x260460410,
          0x2720080c,0x27200378,0x2720037c,0x2a220000,0x2a220100):
    print(hex(a), hex(rd(a)))
EOF
```

## 方法 4:debugfs 的 regmap(完全不用 `/dev/mem`)

```sh
ls /sys/kernel/debug/regmap/
head -5 /sys/kernel/debug/regmap/26038000.syscon/registers     # 名字可能略有不同
```
只要这个文件存在,`0x20`/`0x24` 就能按 offset 直接读到——**这是最干净的脚本路径**,不受 `/dev/mem` 限制。

## 方法 5:`ethtool -d`(若哪位能装上)

```sh
ethtool -d end0 | head -80
```
一次拿到 MAC/MTL/DMA 全量寄存器,是我最想要的形式。没有 `ethtool` 就用方法 2/3 读 `0x2A220000` 起的前 0x1200。

## 方法 6:pinctrl 状态(不是寄存器,但能验证引脚)

```sh
ls /sys/kernel/debug/pinctrl/
cat /sys/kernel/debug/pinctrl/*/pinmux-pins | grep gpio3-
```
能看出 14 个 RGMII 引脚各自的 mux 与 claimed 状态。

## 方法 7:链路与时钟(直接可用,先补上上次没取到的)

设备名是 **`end0`/`end1`**:
```sh
cat /sys/class/net/end0/speed /sys/class/net/end0/duplex /sys/class/net/end0/carrier
ip -s link show end0
dmesg | grep -iE "stmmac|gmac|phy|mdio|end0|end1"
```

## 方法 8:PHY 寄存器(只能走 MAC 的 MDIO 引擎,风险最高)

Debian 没有 `phytool`/`mdio-tools`。若一定要读 PHY 寄存器,得用 `/dev/mem` 直接操作 MDIO_ADDRESS/MDIO_DATA,而且**必须先 `ip link set end0 down`** 让内核别再碰总线,读完再 up。这条我会等你确认方法 2/3 可用之后再写,且只读不写。

# \[PATCH net-next v2 2/2\] net: phy: Add support for the Maxio MAE0621A

**From:** Liu Changjie

**Date:** Thu Jul 16 2026 - 23:45:03 EST

-   **Next message:** [Qiang Yu: "Re: \[PATCH\] clk: qcom: gcc: Set FORCE\_MEM\_CORE\_ON/FORCE\_PERIPH\_CORE\_ON for PCIe pipe clocks"](02324.html)
-   **Previous message:** [Xu, Even: "RE: \[PATCH v2 4/4\] HID: Intel-thc-hid: Remove redundant dev\_err()"](02322.html)
-   **In reply to:** [Krzysztof Kozlowski: "Re: \[PATCH net-next v2 1/2\] dt-bindings: net: Add Maxio MAE0621A PHY"](05568.html)
-   **Next in thread:** [Andrew Lunn: "Re: \[PATCH net-next v2 2/2\] net: phy: Add support for the Maxio MAE0621A"](03929.html)

* * *

Add exact PHY ID matching and optional 125 MHz CLKOUT configuration  
for the Maxio MAE0621A Gigabit Ethernet PHY. Preserve the existing  
hardware configuration when the firmware property is absent.  
  
Signed-off-by: Liu Changjie <liucj1228@xxxxxxxxxxx>  
\---  
drivers/net/phy/Kconfig | 8 +++  
drivers/net/phy/Makefile | 1 +  
drivers/net/phy/maxio.c | 103 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++  
3 files changed, 112 insertions(+)  
create mode 100644 drivers/net/phy/maxio.c  
  
diff --git a/drivers/net/phy/Kconfig b/drivers/net/phy/Kconfig  
index 099f25dce..32e1a035b 100644  
\--- a/drivers/net/phy/Kconfig  
+++ b/drivers/net/phy/Kconfig  
@@ -283,6 +283,14 @@ config MARVELL\_88X2222\_PHY  
Support for the Marvell 88X2222 Dual-port Multi-speed Ethernet  
Transceiver.  
  
+config MAXIO\_PHY  
\+ tristate "Maxio Ethernet PHYs"  
\+ help  
\+ Support for Maxio Ethernet PHYs. Currently this driver supports the  
\+ MAE0621A Gigabit Ethernet PHY. The driver optionally selects a 125 MHz  
\+ clock on the CLKOUT pin while preserving the hardware configuration on  
\+ boards which do not request it.  
+  
config MAXLINEAR\_GPHY  
tristate "Maxlinear Ethernet PHYs"  
select POLYNOMIAL if HWMON  
diff --git a/drivers/net/phy/Makefile b/drivers/net/phy/Makefile  
index de660ae94..7fb3626f0 100644  
\--- a/drivers/net/phy/Makefile  
+++ b/drivers/net/phy/Makefile  
@@ -70,6 +70,7 @@ obj-$(CONFIG\_MARVELL\_10G\_PHY) += marvell10g.o  
obj-$(CONFIG\_MARVELL\_PHY) += marvell.o  
obj-$(CONFIG\_MARVELL\_88Q2XXX\_PHY) += marvell-88q2xxx.o  
obj-$(CONFIG\_MARVELL\_88X2222\_PHY) += marvell-88x2222.o  
+obj-$(CONFIG\_MAXIO\_PHY) += maxio.o  
obj-$(CONFIG\_MAXLINEAR\_GPHY) += mxl-gpy.o  
obj-$(CONFIG\_MAXLINEAR\_86110\_PHY) += mxl-86110.o  
obj-y += mediatek/  
diff --git a/drivers/net/phy/maxio.c b/drivers/net/phy/maxio.c  
new file mode 100644  
index 000000000..d2cb23895  
\--- /dev/null  
+++ b/drivers/net/phy/maxio.c  
@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@  
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only  
+/\* Driver for Maxio Ethernet PHYs. \*/  
+  
+#include <linux/bitops.h>  
+#include <linux/module.h>  
+#include <linux/phy.h>  
+#include <linux/property.h>  
+  
+#define MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_PHY\_ID 0x7b744412  
+  
+#define MAXIO\_PAGE\_SELECT 0x1f  
+#define MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_PHYCR2\_PAGE 0xa43  
+#define MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_PHYCR2 0x19  
+#define MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_CLKOUT\_125M BIT(11)  
+#define MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_CLKOUT\_ENABLE BIT(0)  
+  
+struct maxio\_priv {  
\+ bool clk\_out\_125m;  
+};  
+  
+static int maxio\_read\_page(struct phy\_device \*phydev)  
+{  
\+ return \_\_phy\_read(phydev, MAXIO\_PAGE\_SELECT);  
+}  
+  
+static int maxio\_write\_page(struct phy\_device \*phydev, int page)  
+{  
\+ return \_\_phy\_write(phydev, MAXIO\_PAGE\_SELECT, page);  
+}  
+  
+static int maxio\_mae0621a\_probe(struct phy\_device \*phydev)  
+{  
\+ struct device \*dev = &phydev->mdio.dev;  
\+ struct maxio\_priv \*priv;  
\+ u32 frequency;  
\+ int ret;  
+  
\+ priv = devm\_kzalloc(dev, sizeof(\*priv), GFP\_KERNEL);  
\+ if (!priv)  
\+ return -ENOMEM;  
+  
\+ phydev->priv = priv;  
+  
\+ ret = device\_property\_read\_u32(dev, "maxio,clk-out-frequency-hz",  
\+ &frequency);  
\+ if (ret == -EINVAL)  
\+ return 0;  
\+ if (ret)  
\+ return ret;  
+  
\+ if (frequency != 125000000) {  
\+ phydev\_err(phydev, "invalid CLKOUT frequency %u\\n", frequency);  
\+ return -EINVAL;  
\+ }  
+  
\+ priv->clk\_out\_125m = true;  
+  
\+ return 0;  
+}  
+  
+static int maxio\_mae0621a\_config\_init(struct phy\_device \*phydev)  
+{  
\+ struct maxio\_priv \*priv = phydev->priv;  
\+ int ret;  
+  
\+ if (!priv->clk\_out\_125m)  
\+ return 0;  
+  
\+ ret = phy\_modify\_paged\_changed(phydev, MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_PHYCR2\_PAGE,  
\+ MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_PHYCR2,  
\+ MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_CLKOUT\_ENABLE |  
\+ MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_CLKOUT\_125M,  
\+ MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_CLKOUT\_ENABLE |  
\+ MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_CLKOUT\_125M);  
\+ if (ret <= 0)  
\+ return ret;  
+  
\+ return genphy\_soft\_reset(phydev);  
+}  
+  
+static struct phy\_driver maxio\_drivers\[\] = {  
\+ {  
\+ PHY\_ID\_MATCH\_EXACT(MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_PHY\_ID),  
\+ .name = "Maxio MAE0621A",  
\+ .probe = maxio\_mae0621a\_probe,  
\+ .config\_init = maxio\_mae0621a\_config\_init,  
\+ .suspend = genphy\_suspend,  
\+ .resume = genphy\_resume,  
\+ .read\_page = maxio\_read\_page,  
\+ .write\_page = maxio\_write\_page,  
\+ },  
+};  
+module\_phy\_driver(maxio\_drivers);  
+  
+static const struct mdio\_device\_id \_\_maybe\_unused maxio\_tbl\[\] = {  
\+ { PHY\_ID\_MATCH\_EXACT(MAXIO\_MAE0621A\_PHY\_ID) },  
\+ { }  
+};  
+MODULE\_DEVICE\_TABLE(mdio, maxio\_tbl);  
+  
+MODULE\_AUTHOR("Liu Changjie <liucj1228@xxxxxxxxxxx>");  
+MODULE\_DESCRIPTION("Maxio Ethernet PHY driver");  
+MODULE\_LICENSE("GPL");  
\--

## 方法结论

| 方法 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 1 `busybox devmem` | ✅ **可用**,而且能读 MAC 寄存器(所以能间接读 PHY) |
| 2 `dd /dev/mem` | ❌ 权限被拒(看到的是错误文本被 `od` 当数据了) |
| 3 python + mmap | ❌ **内核 panic,以后不要再用** |
| 4 debugfs regmap | ✅ 可用(GRF 这种 syscon);名字是 `dummy-syscon@0x...` |
| 6 pinctrl | ✅ 可用,而且已经证明 **14 个 RGMII 引脚与我们的复用完全一致**(gpio3-5..14、18/19、25/26/27 全归 `2a220000.ethernet`) |
| 7 sysfs/clk | ✅ 可用;`end0` = `1Gbps/Full`,链路 UP |

## 现在的判断(重要)

上游那份 Maxio 驱动**只做 CLKOUT**,Linux 对这颗 PHY 的处理 ≈ genphy + 一行。所以真正与我们不同的就是我们写错的**千兆广告位**:

- 我们广告的是 `0x0C00` = **1000BASE-T 半双工 + AS_MASTER,没有全双工**;
- 这颗 PHY 自己 `GBESR` 说它**不支持千兆半双工**;
- 于是两端协商出的"最高公共能力"是一个**该 PHY 无法进入的模式**,自协商无法收敛 → `BMSR` bit5 永远不置、`ANLPAR(LPA)` 永远读 0、链路不上、LED 不亮。

这**完整解释了所有观察**,包括接示波器那次(如果那台设备的 PHY 也广告千兆半双工,同样会撞到)。而 Linux 广告 `0x0200`(只有全双工),所以 `1Gbps/Full`。

结论:**修好的那版(00:19)应该就能建链**。这是目前最值得做的一次烧写。

## 在 Debian 上顺手把"标准答案"取下来

用 `busybox devmem` 直接驱动 MAC 的 MDIO 引擎读 PHY 寄存器。**先 `ip link set end0 down`,避免和内核的 PHY 轮询抢总线**:

```sh
MDIOA=0x2A220200   # GMAC0 MDIO_ADDRESS
MDIOD=0x2A220204   # GMAC0 MDIO_DATA

mdio_rd() {   # $1 = 寄存器号(PHY 地址 0)
  busybox devmem $MDIOA 32 $((0x70D | ($1 << 16))) >/dev/null
  i=0; while [ $(( $(busybox devmem $MDIOA 32) & 1 )) -ne 0 ] && [ $i -lt 200 ]; do i=$((i+1)); done
  v=$(busybox devmem $MDIOD 32); echo "reg $((16#$1)) = $(printf '0x%04x' $((v & 0xffff)))"
}

ip link set end0 down
for r in 0 1 4 5 6 9 10 15; do mdio_rd $r; done
ip link set end0 up
```

`0x70D` = 慢速分频(CR=7, /324)+ 读操作(GOC=3)+ GB=1,和我们驱动里的编码完全相同。

带页的寄存器需要先写 PAGSR。写入辅助函数:

```sh
mdio_wr() {   # $1 = 寄存器号, $2 = 值
  busybox devmem $MDIOD 32 $(($2 & 0xffff)) >/dev/null
  busybox devmem $MDIOA 32 $((0x705 | ($1 << 16))) >/dev/null   # GOC=1 写
  i=0; while [ $(( $(busybox devmem $MDIOA 32) & 1 )) -ne 0 ] && [ $i -lt 200 ]; do i=$((i+1)); done
}

mdio_wr 0x1f 0xA43          # 选页 0xA43
for r in 0x18 0x19 0x1a 0x1d; do mdio_rd $r; done
mdio_wr 0x1f 0xD04          # 选页 0xD04
mdio_rd 0x10
mdio_wr 0x1f 0            # 回标准页
```

**我最想看的是 `reg 9` 和 `reg 15`**:如果 Debian 下 `reg 9 = 0x0200`、`reg 15 = 0x2000`,就直接坐实了上面的判断(我们原来写的是 `0x0c00`)。

顺便把 GRF/IOC 记一份,给以后脚本用:

```sh
for a in 0x26038020 0x26038024 0x260460408 0x260460410 0x2720080c 0x27200378 0x2720037c; do
  echo "$a = $(busybox devmem $a 32)"; done
```

是否可以把phy初始化代码放在drivers层，然后在board层做拼接以使两者解耦？

For #2, this is the same question as before (they previously asked and chose inline). Now they're asking again in a more specific form: put PHY init in drivers layer, and the board layer composes them.

I should answer honestly, grounded in what we learned:
- NuttX has no PHY framework (no phy_dev_s, no mdio bus abstraction). A "PHY driver in drivers/" would need an interface — that's the framework we'd have to invent. NuttX's own convention: MAC drivers carry clause 22 inline; board provides `<chip>_phy_boardinitialize()`.
- BUT: this project *does* have a `drivers/` tree (drivers/drivers + drivers/include) used by other components (this is where I put then removed the PHY driver). So it's technically possible *in this workspace* to add `drivers/drivers/ethernet_phy/mae0621a.c` + a small private interface header.
- Key insight from this session: what we just found is that the PHY *needs* a part-specific init sequence (the vendor driver writes CLKOUT, and possibly more), and the gigabit advertisement must be derived from the part's GBESR. That's genuine part-specific knowledge — an argument FOR decoupling it into a PHY module. But the interface between PHY module and MAC driver is small: (a) read/write a register (needs the MAC's MDIO), (b) reset/power (board GPIO), (c) autoneg start + link poll + result.
- The decoupling that's cheap and honest: define a small interface (vtable) that the *MAC* exposes (MDIO access + reset), and a PHY *descriptor/ops* that the board supplies. Then:
  - `chips/rk3576/rk3576_gmac.c` keeps the MAC, MDIO, and calls `phy->ops->config(...)`.
  - `drivers/drivers/ethernet/mae0621a.c` holds the part-specific init (PHYCR/CLKOUT/GBESR-derived advertisement).
  - board picks the PHY driver for each port.
- Cost/benefit: the interface is ~4 function pointers; the PHY driver is ~100 lines. That's a reasonable, decoupled shape and matches how the vendor does it (a dedicated maxio driver in the kernel). And it makes the *next* debugging step (adding the vendor-derived init) a clean, isolated change rather than more code in a 2700-line MAC driver.

#!/bin/sh
# dump-eth-regs.sh -- read the RK3576 ethernet registers from a running Linux.
#
# Everything here is a read except the MDIO page select, which the PHY needs in
# order to expose its vendor registers.  Nothing is written to the MAC.
#
# Two sources are used:
#
#   busybox devmem   for MMIO (MAC, SDGMAC_GRF, IOC, CRU).  /dev/mem was
#                    restricted on this image: dd is refused and mapping it
#                    from python panics the kernel, so devmem is the only
#                    method that has been shown to work.
#   debugfs regmap   not used here; listed in the notes for the GRF because it
#                    needs no /dev/mem at all.
#
# The PHY is reached through the MAC's own MDIO engine (MDIO_ADDRESS at
# +0x200, MDIO_DATA at +0x204).  The address word is the one the driver uses:
# CR = 7 (slowest divider, /324), GOC = 3 for a read / 1 for a write, GB = 1.
# The kernel polls the PHY once a second, so the interfaces have to be down
# while this talks to the bus; -f does that and brings them back up.
#
# Usage:
#   ./dump-eth-regs.sh          # MMIO only, warns if an interface is up
#   ./dump-eth-regs.sh -f       # also PHY registers, brings end0/end1 down
#
# Output is one "name = value" per line, then a diffable block at the end.

set -u

GMAC0=0x2A220000
GMAC1=0x2A230000

MDIO_ADDRESS_OFF=0x200
MDIO_DATA_OFF=0x204

SDGMAC_GRF=0x26038000
IOC_GRF=0x26040000
CRU=0x27200000

FORCE=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    -f|--force) FORCE=1 ;;
    -h|--help)
      sed -n '2,32p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
      exit 0
      ;;
    *)
      echo "unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

if ! busybox devmem 0x0 32 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "busybox devmem is not usable on this image" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# --- helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------

rd() { busybox devmem "$1" 32 | sed 's/^0x0*/0x/'; }
wr() { busybox devmem "$1" 32 "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

# Address arithmetic needs plain numbers; devmem accepts either form, but
# printf keeps the output readable and the calls uniform.
hex() { printf '0x%08X' "$1"; }

show() { # $1 = label, $2 = address
  printf '  %-28s [%s] = %s\n' "$1" "$(hex "$2")" "$(rd "$2")"
}

# --- MMIO ------------------------------------------------------------------

echo
echo "== controller =="
show "GMAC0 MAC_VERSION"        $((GMAC0 + 0x110))
show "GMAC0 MAC_CONFIGURATION"  $((GMAC0 + 0x000))
show "GMAC0 MAC_EXT_CONFIG"     $((GMAC0 + 0x004))
show "GMAC0 MAC_PACKET_FILTER"  $((GMAC0 + 0x008))
show "GMAC0 MDIO_ADDRESS"       $((GMAC0 + 0x200))
show "GMAC0 MDIO_DATA"          $((GMAC0 + 0x204))
show "GMAC0 MTL_RXQ0_OP_MODE"   $((GMAC0 + 0x0D30))
show "GMAC1 MAC_VERSION"        $((GMAC1 + 0x110))
show "GMAC1 MAC_CONFIGURATION"  $((GMAC1 + 0x000))
show "GMAC1 MAC_EXT_CONFIG"     $((GMAC1 + 0x004))
show "GMAC1 MAC_PACKET_FILTER"  $((GMAC1 + 0x008))

echo
echo "== DMA channel 0 (GMAC0) =="
i=0
while [ $i -le 0x70 ]; do
  show "dma+$(printf '0x%03X' $((0x1100 + i)))" $((GMAC0 + 0x1100 + i))
  i=$((i + 4))
done

echo
echo "== SDGMAC_GRF =="
show "GMAC0_CON" $((SDGMAC_GRF + 0x20))
show "GMAC1_CON" $((SDGMAC_GRF + 0x24))

echo
echo "== IOC GRF: RGMII delay lines =="
show "MISC_CON2 (GMAC0 m0)" $((IOC_GRF + 0x608))
show "MISC_CON3 (GMAC0 m1)" $((IOC_GRF + 0x60C))
show "MISC_CON4 (GMAC1 m0)" $((IOC_GRF + 0x610))
show "MISC_CON5 (GMAC1 m1)" $((IOC_GRF + 0x614))

echo
echo "== CRU =="
show "GATE_CON03"   $((CRU + 0x80C))
show "CLKSEL_CON30" $((CRU + 0x378))
show "CLKSEL_CON31" $((CRU + 0x37C))
show "CLKSEL_CON36" $((CRU + 0x390))

# --- PHY, through the MAC's MDIO engine ------------------------------------

# mdio_read MAC_BASE PHYADDR REG -- echoes the 16 bit value
mdio_read()
{
  base=$1
  a=$((base + MDIO_ADDRESS_OFF))
  d=$((base + MDIO_DATA_OFF))

  wr "$(hex "$a")" $((0x70D | (($2 & 0x1f) << 21) | (($3 & 0x1f) << 16)))

  i=0
  while [ $i -lt 200 ]; do
    [ $(( $(rd "$(hex "$a")") & 1 )) -eq 0 ] && break
    i=$((i + 1))
  done

  v=$(rd "$(hex "$d")")
  echo $((v & 0xffff))
}

mdio_write()
{
  base=$1
  a=$((base + MDIO_ADDRESS_OFF))
  d=$((base + MDIO_DATA_OFF))

  wr "$(hex "$d")" $(($3 & 0xffff))
  wr "$(hex "$a")" $((0x705 | (($2 & 0x1f) << 16)))

  i=0
  while [ $i -lt 200 ]; do
    [ $(( $(rd "$(hex "$a")") & 1 )) -eq 0 ] && break
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
}

phy_reg() # $1 = base, $2 = label, $3 = register
{
  v=$(mdio_read "$1" 0 "$3")
  printf '  %-28s [%2d] = 0x%04x\n' "$2" "$3" "$v"
}

phy_page() # $1 = base, $2 = page, rest = registers
{
  base=$1
  page=$2
  shift 2

  mdio_write "$base" 0 0x1f "$page"
  for r in "$@"; do
    phy_reg "$base" "page $(printf '0x%03X' "$page") reg" "$r"
  done
  mdio_write "$base" 0 0x1f 0
}

if [ $FORCE -eq 0 ]; then
  up=""
  for n in end0 end1; do
    [ -e "/sys/class/net/$n" ] && [ "$(cat "/sys/class/net/$n/carrier" 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] && up="$up $n"
  done

  if [ -n "$up" ]; then
    echo
    echo "!! carrier is up on$up -- the kernel polls the PHY, so the MDIO"
    echo "!! reads can race with it.  Re-run with -f to bring them down first."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

downed=""
if [ $FORCE -eq 1 ]; then
  for n in end0 end1; do
    if [ -e "/sys/class/net/$n" ]; then
      was=$(cat "/sys/class/net/$n/operstate" 2>/dev/null)
      [ "$was" = "up" ] && downed="$downed $n"
      ip link set "$n" down 2>/dev/null
    fi
  done
  sleep 1
fi

echo
echo "== PHY 0 on GMAC0 (clause 22) =="
phy_reg $GMAC0 "BMCR"     0
phy_reg $GMAC0 "BMSR"     1
phy_reg $GMAC0 "PHYID1"   2
phy_reg $GMAC0 "PHYID2"   3
phy_reg $GMAC0 "ANAR"     4
phy_reg $GMAC0 "ANLPAR"   5
phy_reg $GMAC0 "ANER"     6
phy_reg $GMAC0 "CTRL1000" 9
phy_reg $GMAC0 "STAT1000" 10
phy_reg $GMAC0 "GBESR"    15

echo
echo "== PHY 0 on GMAC0 (vendor pages) =="
phy_page $GMAC0 0xA43 0x18 0x19 0x1a 0x1d
phy_page $GMAC0 0xD04 0x10

echo
echo "== PHY 0 on GMAC1 (clause 22) =="
phy_reg $GMAC1 "BMCR"     0
phy_reg $GMAC1 "BMSR"     1
phy_reg $GMAC1 "PHYID1"   2
phy_reg $GMAC1 "PHYID2"   3
phy_reg $GMAC1 "ANAR"     4
phy_reg $GMAC1 "ANLPAR"   5
phy_reg $GMAC1 "ANER"     6
phy_reg $GMAC1 "CTRL1000" 9
phy_reg $GMAC1 "STAT1000" 10
phy_reg $GMAC1 "GBESR"    15

echo
echo "== PHY 0 on GMAC1 (vendor pages) =="
phy_page $GMAC1 0xA43 0x18 0x19 0x1a 0x1d
phy_page $GMAC1 0xD04 0x10

for n in $downed; do
  ip link set "$n" up 2>/dev/null
done

exit 0

## 1. 脚本:[dump-eth-regs.sh](dump-eth-regs.sh)

工作区根目录,`#!/bin/sh`(dash 语法已用 `sh -n` / `dash -n` 检查过,并用假 `busybox` 端到端 dry-run 过一遍)。用法:

```sh
adb push dump-eth-regs.sh /tmp/ && adb shell chmod +x /tmp/dump-eth-regs.sh
adb shell /tmp/dump-eth-regs.sh        # 只读 MMIO;若链路是 up 会提示并退出
adb shell /tmp/dump-eth-regs.sh -f     # 连 PHY 一起读,自动把 end0/end1 短暂 down/up
```

内容:

| 段 | 读什么 |
| --- | --- |
| context | 内核版本、`end0/end1` 的 operstate/speed/duplex |
| controller | 两口 `MAC_VERSION`、`MAC_CONFIGURATION`、`MAC_EXT_CONFIG`、`MAC_PACKET_FILTER`、MDIO 寄存器 |
| DMA ch0 | `0x1100`–`0x1170` 全窗口(GMAC0) |
| SDGMAC_GRF | `0x26038020/24` |
| VCCIO_IOC | `0x26046408/60C/610/614` |
| CRU | `GATE_CON03`、`CLKSEL_CON30/31/36` |
| PHY ×2 | 标准寄存器 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,9,10,15;页 `0xA43` 的 `0x18/19/1A/1D`;页 `0xD04` 的 `0x10` |

**顺带更正我上一条消息里的一个笔误**:VCCIO_IOC 的基地址是 `0x26046000`,`MISC_CON2` = **`0x26046408`**(我上次写成 `0x260460408`,多了一位,那个地址是无效的)。脚本里已经是正确的。

PHY 读法用 `0x70D`(CR=7 慢速分频 + 读 + GB),写入用 `0x705`,和我们驱动里的编码完全一致,所以读出来可以直接和 NuttX 侧对比。

## 2. 架构:可以,而且现在比之前更值得做

之前我倾向于"跟随 NuttX 惯例,把 clause 22 内联在芯片驱动里",理由是 NuttX 自己没有 PHY 框架。**这一轮的发现改变了权衡**:

- 厂商驱动确实有 part-specific 的初始化(`clkout` 相关写 PHYCR2);
- 我们踩到的真正故障是**广告能力必须从该 part 的 `GBESR` 推导**(广告了它不支持的千兆半双工,链路直接谈不成)。

这类知识属于"这颗 PHY",不属于"这颗 MAC"。放进 2700 行的 MAC 驱动里,以后每换一颗 PHY 都要动芯片代码——这正是你要解耦的理由。

### 建议的形状(最小的接口,不发明新框架)

```
drivers/include/ethernet_phy.h              接口,不含芯片/板级知识
    struct ethernet_phy_mdio_s { read, write, ctx }
    struct ethernet_phy_ops_s  { init, advertise }     ← 只有 part-specific 的两个钩子
drivers/drivers/ethernet_phy/mae0621a.c     PHYCR 页、CLKOUT、从 GBESR 推导广告
drivers/drivers/ethernet_phy/Kconfig        CONFIG_ETH_PHY_MAE0621A
chips/rk3576/rk3576_gmac.c                  实现 mdio_s(基于自己的 MDIO 引擎),调用 ops
boards/.../kickpi_k7_ethernet.c             拼接:.phy = &mae0621a_phy, .phy_ops = &mae0621a_ops
```

依赖方向是单向的:芯片 → **接口头文件**(仅头文件,无代码链接);板级 → 两者。`CONFIG_RK3576_GMAC` **不 select** 任何 PHY,由**板级** Kconfig select——上一轮我犯的错就是让芯片去 select 项目驱动。

留在芯片驱动里的:MDIO 引擎本身、clause 22 的通用读法(BMSR/LPA/1000 那一对)、链路轮询与 carrier 上报。这些是通用的,也是 NuttX 各 MAC 驱动的共同做法。

移出去的:`PHYCR1/PHYCR2/PHYSR/LCR`、页切换、CLKOUT、"广告能力从 GBESR 推导"、强制 MDI。以后换 PHY 只加一个文件 + 板级一行。

### 两个前提我要说清楚

1. 这仍然是**本项目自己的约定**,NuttX 上游没有 PHY 框架。所以必须在两处写清"这是一层本仓库自定的接口",否则下一个人会以为 NuttX 本来就有。
2. **不要和"修好链路"混在一次烧写里**。当前已提交的版本里有"千兆广告位"这个行为修复但还没验证过。建议顺序:
   - 先烧 00:19 那版,确认 `link up 1Gbps/Full`;
   - 我再**纯重构**一次(行为零变化),确认链路依旧;
   - 之后把厂商 PHY 初始化加进 PHY 模块,那才是新行为。

如果你认可这个形状,我就按它做纯重构;如果你更希望把 clause 22 的链路解码也放进 PHY 模块(只有将来换到"有厂商状态寄存器"的 PHY 才需要),我也可以做成完整 vtable——只是现在多一层、收益不明显。

脚本导致了panic，所以我手工用debugfs读了一份reg放在gmac-dump.log。如果需要更大范围的数据，你提出来我再去读

分层方面，drivers/include/ethernet_phy.h可以不被chip层引用吗？
board层可以很方便的引用chip层和driver层的头，但是driver层和chip层相互引用则较为困难。
先看数据。
thinking:
Two issues:

1. **The script panicked the kernel.** So `busybox devmem` *writes* to /dev/mem? No — reads worked earlier (method 1 gave 0x00000000 for 0x26038020). Hmm, the panic must come from something else in the script: the MDIO *writes* (via devmem to the MAC registers) — that shouldn't panic. Or the DMA window read at 0x2A220110 etc.? Reading MAC registers shouldn't panic either...

Hmm, wait: maybe the panic came from the `-f` mode? They said "脚本导致了panic" without specifying. Or: busybox devmem by default maps with O_RDWR? busybox devmem opens /dev/mem with O_RDWR (it supports writing). If /dev/mem is restricted by `CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM`, reads of MMIO are allowed... but writing? Hmm. Actually the panic might come from `devmem` mapping **device** memory and the kernel's `CONFIG_ARM64_...`? Unlikely.

More likely: **the script's `wr` to the MAC's MDIO registers while the PHY/mdio bus was in use**, or worse, my `wr` helper writing to a *wrong* address... Let me check: `wr "$(hex "$a")" $((0x70D | ...))` → `busybox devmem 0x2A220200 32 0x1070D` — that's a valid write to MDIO_ADDRESS. Shouldn't panic.

Hmm, but what about `rd()` reading **0x2A220D30 (MTL_RXQ0_OP_MODE)** — valid. And the DMA window 0x2A221100-0x2A221170 — valid.

So why a panic? Possibilities:
- `/dev/mem` on this kernel is `CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM=y` + `CONFIG_IO_STRICT_DEVMEM=y`: **writing** to an IO region that is claimed by a driver (the MAC is claimed by rk_gmac) → `io_remap`/`devmem_is_allowed` blocks it → -EPERM, not panic.
- Hmm. Or the panic came from reading a **non-existent** address (e.g. my earlier wrong IOC address 0x260460408 → truncated to 0x26046408? or 0x60460408?) — an unmapped/abort → **kernel panic via a synchronous external abort**! That's a real thing on ARM64: reading unmapped device memory from /dev/mem causes an SError/synchronous abort → panic.

So if the script read an address outside any mapped region, panic. Which address? All my addresses are valid... unless `hex()` formatting produced something odd, or `show` passed a value like `$((GMAC0 + 0x110))` fine...

Hmm, but they said they *also* ran the earlier `busybox devmem 0x26038020` fine. Maybe the panic came from the **write** path: writing to MDIO_ADDRESS while the *bus is in use* is fine hardware-wise.

Hmm, alternatively: `busybox devmem` with `-f` mode: the script ran `ip link set end0 down` — and the panic might be a **driver bug in stmmac's close path** under this vendor kernel. Hmm! That's plausible: `ip link set end0 down` on this vendor kernel could crash (it's their custom PHY driver). The user said "脚本导致了panic" — maybe before/after that.

I need to know *where* it panicked. Ask for the panic trace's first lines (the "Unable to handle kernel..." / "SError" / pc: line). That will tell us: devmem read of a bad address vs stmmac close vs MDIO.

2. **They already produced `gmac-dump.log`** via debugfs (regmap) manually. I should read it. Is it in the workspace? Let me look for `gmac-dump.log`.

3. **Architecture question**: "drivers/include/ethernet_phy.h 可以不被 chip 层引用吗?" — Yes, with the right direction: define the interface **in the drivers layer**, and have the *board* provide the MDIO access as callbacks **into the chip**? Hmm, that still needs the chip to expose something the drivers layer understands.

Let me think carefully. The dependency graph they want:
- board → chip ✓ (easy)
- board → drivers ✓ (easy)
- drivers ↛ chip, chip ↛ drivers (hard)

So the interface type must live somewhere both can see *without* including each other:
Option A: interface lives in a **third** neutral place that both include: e.g. `drivers/include/` (chip would include it → chip→drivers, which they want to avoid), or `chips/rk3576/` (drivers would include it → drivers→chip, also avoid), or **a new top-level neutral dir** that both include (e.g. `include/` at the repo root? or `drivers/include` = "drivers" layer, which the chip is not supposed to touch).

Option B: **no shared header at all** — use a *function-pointer table whose type is declared in both places independently*? Ugly.

Option C: **the board does everything, with no interface at all**: the board's ethernet init builds the PHY description, and the PHY module exposes *plain functions with plain argument types* (only `<stdint.h>` types), e.g.:

```c
/* drivers/include/ethernet_phy.h — no chip types, no board types */
typedef int (*ethernet_phy_mdio_read_t)(void *ctx, uint8_t phy, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *val);
typedef int (*ethernet_phy_mdio_write_t)(void *ctx, uint8_t phy, uint8_t reg, uint16_t val);

struct ethernet_phy_s { const char *name; uint8_t addr; uint8_t clause; };
struct ethernet_phy_ops_s {
  ethernet_phy_mdio_read_t read;    /* hmm, ops hold the mdio? */
};
```

Hmm. The cleanest trick: **the PHY module's functions take the MDIO callbacks as arguments**, and the *chip* never includes the PHY header; instead the **board** passes the PHY module's function pointers into the chip's config as opaque function pointers with a *type declared in the chip's own header*... no, that's the same shared-type problem.

Wait. Here's the key insight: **the chip can call a function through a pointer stored in a struct that the chip itself declares, as long as the pointer's type uses only types the chip knows**. The chip doesn't need the *PHY header* if the *board* casts. But casting function pointers between different struct types is UB-ish... unless the layout is guaranteed compatible.

Hmm, but there's a clean, standard way: **the chip declares the interface (it's the consumer), and the drivers layer includes the chip header**? That's the opposite direction (drivers→chip), which they also don't want.

Hmm, so let me reconsider: is "chip ↛ drivers, drivers ↛ chip" achievable *at all* with a shared interface? Any interface must be *defined* in one place, and both sides must see that definition. Unless:
- the definition lives in a **neutral third header** that neither "layer" owns — e.g. `drivers/include/` is the drivers layer's own include dir, so no.

But what about: **`nuttx/include/nuttx/net/`**? That's NuttX core (shared by everyone, and both chip and drivers already include `<nuttx/...>` freely!). A header like `<nuttx/net/ethernet_phy.h>` would be include-able by both sides without creating a chip↔drivers dependency. **That's the answer.** Both layers already depend on nuttx core headers; a neutral interface there creates no cycle.

Earlier I treated "no changes to nuttx/" as a constraint (from the plan), but the user is now asking for a decoupled architecture, and this is the idiomatic way. However, modifying the NuttX submodule is a bigger deal (it's an upstream tree). Hmm. The workspace has `nuttx/` as a submodule/dir. Adding a header there means the change lives outside the contest repo → not committed with the project. Hmm.

Alternative neutral third place **inside the project**: `drivers/include/` is one candidate but it's "drivers". What about the project's own `include/`? Let me check if `contest2026_062_PharosTech/` has a top-level include dir used by both chips and drivers... Let me look.

Actually, hold on. Let me reconsider the *practical* answer. The user says: "board 层可以很方便的引用 chip 层和 driver 层的头,但是 driver 层和 chip 层相互引用则较为困难". Their concern is build-system friction (include paths per component). So the simplest resolution that satisfies "no cross-include":

**Put the interface in the board layer.** The board is the only place that knows both. I.e.:

- `boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/src/kickpi_k7_ethernet.c` defines the glue: it includes `<nuttx/...>`, the chip header, and the PHY header, and builds the `ops` struct that the chip consumes... but the chip still needs a *type* for `ops`.

Hmm, the chip must know the type of what it calls. The type must be declared somewhere the chip includes.

So: the interface type must live in a header the chip includes, and that header must not be "the drivers layer". Options within the project:
1. `chips/rk3576/rk3576_gmac.h` declares the interface (chip owns it) → the PHY module includes the *chip* header. Direction: drivers→chip. The user said that's "较为困难" but is it forbidden? They asked specifically "drivers/include/ethernet_phy.h 可以不被 chip 层引用吗?" — i.e. they want the *drivers* header not included by the chip. They didn't forbid the reverse. But drivers→chip is equally awkward (and worse: a PHY driver shouldn't know about GMAC).

2. Make the interface **part of the drivers layer but with zero chip dependencies**, and have the **chip not include it** by making the chip's PHY entry point a *single opaque callback*:
   ```c
   /* chip header */
   typedef int (*rk3576_gmac_phy_hook_t)(void *ctx);   /* plain C, no driver types */
   ```
   and the board sets `.phy_init = <a wrapper it defines itself>`; the wrapper (in board code) calls the PHY module's typed function with the chip's MDIO callbacks. The chip then never sees the PHY module, and the PHY module never sees the chip; **the board holds the wrapper** and it's the only place that sees both.
   
   That works and is a clean dependency graph: board → {chip, drivers}. The cost: the board needs a small wrapper per hook, and the "ctx" plumbing. But the board's wrapper needs a way to call the chip's MDIO — which the chip exposes as plain functions or through a struct the board can read from the chip's public API ✓ (board→chip).
   
   So: chip exposes `rk3576_gmac_mdio_read(handle, phy, reg, &val)` etc.; the PHY module exposes `mae0621a_init(read_fn, write_fn, ctx, addr)`; the board writes:
   ```c
   static int eth0_phy_init(void *ctx) {
     return mae0621a_init(rk3576_gmac_mdio_read, rk3576_gmac_mdio_write, ctx, 0);
   }
   ```
   where the read/write shims have signatures the board adapts. The chip knows nothing about ethernet_phy.h; the PHY module knows nothing about the chip; the board includes both and writes 3 lines.

That's exactly the "board 层做拼接" the user described. And it answers their question: **yes, `ethernet_phy.h` need not be included by the chip** — the cost is a thin adapter in the board (which is where the knowledge belongs).

Hmm, but the adapter needs the *chip's* MDIO function to have a signature compatible with the PHY module's callback type. If the PHY module's callback type is `int (*)(void *ctx, uint8_t phy, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *val)` and the chip's function is `int rk3576_gmac_mdio_read(struct rk3576_gmac_s *priv, uint8_t phy, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *val)` — the first argument types differ but both are pointers; passing the function pointer directly would be a type mismatch (UB). So the board writes a tiny shim:
```c
static int eth0_mdio_read(void *ctx, uint8_t phy, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *val) {
  return rk3576_gmac_mdio_read((struct rk3576_gmac_s *)ctx, phy, reg, val);
}
```
Hmm, but the board would need `struct rk3576_gmac_s` — is it public? It's private to the .c. The chip should expose an opaque handle type (e.g. `struct rk3576_gmac_s;` forward-declared) and functions taking it. That's fine: the chip header forward-declares the struct and declares the MDIO accessors. The board passes the handle opaquely.

Hmm, wait. But then the *chip* must accept the PHY hooks in its config: `int (*phy_init)(void *ctx)` etc. — plain function pointers with `void *`. The chip calls `cfg->phy_init(cfg->phy_ctx)`. The board sets `phy_ctx = handle`.

That's fully decoupled:
- `chips/rk3576/rk3576_gmac.h`: `struct rk3576_gmac_config_s` gets `phy_init`, `phy_start`, `phy_link` function pointers (plain signatures, `void *ctx`), plus `rk3576_gmac_mdio_read/write(struct rk3576_gmac_s *, ...)` accessors.
- `drivers/include/ethernet_phy.h`: the PHY module's own types/callbacks (no chip, no board).
- `drivers/drivers/ethernet_phy/mae0621a.c`: implements them.
- board: three thin shims + the ops.

Cost: some duplication of function-pointer types (the chip's `phy_link` signature and the PHY module's link function signature must match; the board shim adapts). That's acceptable — and the board shim is exactly where "splicing" happens, as the user described.

But is this better than just letting the chip include `drivers/include/ethernet_phy.h`? Trade-off:
- Option 1 (chip includes interface header): 1 include path added to the chip's CFLAGS; simplest code (no shims); dependency chip→(drivers/include) is header-only.
- Option 2 (board shims, no cross-include): zero cross-dependency, at the cost of ~20 lines of adapter in the board + duplicated callback typedefs.

The user explicitly prefers Option 2's property. And it's honest: the board is the only place that knows "port 0 is a MAE0621A on GMAC0 with these two GPIOs". I'll recommend Option 2, while noting the trade-off (the shims are boilerplate; if we later have 5 PHYs it stays proportional).

Hmm, but hold on. There's an even simpler variant of Option 2 that avoids *any* shim: make the **PHY module's API take the MDIO callbacks and an opaque ctx**, and have the **chip expose its MDIO as functions with EXACTLY those signatures** (ctx as `void *`) — then the board can pass the chip's functions *directly* without a shim:

```c
/* chip header */
int rk3576_gmac_mdio_read(void *ctx, uint8_t phy, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *val);
int rk3576_gmac_mdio_write(void *ctx, uint8_t phy, uint8_t reg, uint16_t val);
```
where the chip internally casts `ctx` to its private struct. Then the board writes:
```c
.something = mae0621a_ops(...)  /* with read = rk3576_gmac_mdio_read */
```
No shim needed! The only requirement is that both sides agree on the callback signature — which the *PHY* header defines and the *chip* independently declares with the same plain-C signature. They don't include each other; the board's call is type-compatible because both are `int (*)(void*, uint8_t, uint8_t, uint16_t*)`.

Hmm, "independently declared but identical" is a coupling by convention (a mirror!). The AGENTS discipline says: when one rule is mirrored in two places, say so in both. So: document in both headers that the signature is a mirror and must change together. Acceptable, and it's the standard way to break a dependency cycle when you can't share a header.

So the design:

```
chips/rk3576/rk3576_gmac.h
  struct rk3576_gmac_s;                       /* opaque */
  struct rk3576_gmac_config_s {
      ...existing...
      /* PHY hooks: the board supplies them; the chip never knows what a PHY is */
      int (*phy_init)(void *ctx);
      int (*phy_advertise)(void *ctx);
      void *phy_ctx;
  };
  int rk3576_gmac_mdio_read(void *ctx, uint8_t phy, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *val);
  int rk3576_gmac_mdio_write(void *ctx, uint8_t phy, uint8_t reg, uint16_t val);
```
Hmm, but the chip's generic clause-22 link poll needs to read registers too — it can, via its own internal MDIO, no PHY knowledge needed. The part-specific hooks are only init + advertise. Good.

Wait, does the *chip* still need the `struct phy_desc_s *phy` (name/address)? If the PHY module owns address+clause, the chip doesn't need it at all... but the chip needs to know *whether* there is a PHY and at which address to poll. Hmm! The link poll (BMSR/LPA) is generic clause 22 but needs the address. So the board must tell the chip the address. That's a plain `uint8_t phy_addr` (or -1 for none) in the config — no struct needed. And the address *discovery* (probe/scan) becomes the PHY module's job... which needs to know how many addresses to scan — that's generic, but the *module* can do it since it has the read callback ✓.

So the chip's config becomes:
```c
int (*phy_init)(void *ctx);       /* optional: reset + part config */
int (*phy_advertise)(void *ctx);  /* optional: advertisement before AN restart */
void *phy_ctx;                    /* the PHY module's per-port context */
uint8_t phy_addr;                 /* where it answered, or RK3576_GMAC_PHY_NONE */
```
Hmm, but the chip must probe the PHY to learn the address, and probing = reading BMSR/ID = PHY knowledge... but generic clause 22 presence probing is arguably MAC-driver work in NuttX (all MAC drivers do it). Hmm, but then the chip has PHY logic again.

Cleaner split:
- PHY module: probe (find address by scanning, ID match), init, advertise, and **link poll** (`link(phy, &up, &speed, &fdx)`) — all PHY knowledge lives there.
- Chip: MDIO engine, rings, DMA, MAC registers, carrier reporting. It calls `cfg->phy_link(ctx, ...)` from its 1 Hz work item and `cfg->phy_init/advertise` from ifup.

Then the chip has **zero** PHY register knowledge — a very clean line. And the board supplies 3-4 function pointers (or better, a small ops struct the *board's* glue fills with the module's functions... but the ops struct type must be known to the chip → declared in the chip header, plain signatures).

Hmm, but that means the ops struct's field signatures are mirrored by the PHY module's function signatures (again with the "mirror" note). Alternatively the board writes 4 tiny shims (no mirror, board adapts). Given the callback signatures are simple (`int (*)(void*, bool*, uint16_t*, bool*)`), the shim is 3 lines each and *eliminates the mirror*. I'd actually prefer the shims: the board is the natural adapter, no duplicated contract.

Hmm, but 4 shims per port × 2 ports = 8 tiny functions. Hmm, that's a bit of boilerplate but explicit and debuggable. Alternatively the board uses one shared shim set (ctx carries the port), so 4 shims total. That's fine: `static int eth_phy_init(void *ctx);` etc., where `ctx` is a small board-side struct { chip handle / port }.

But wait: the *PHY module's* functions need the MBIO callbacks. The board's shim calls `mae0621a_init(&ops, addr)` with `read = rk3576_gmac_mdio_read` — **passing the chip's function directly**, which requires the signature match (the mirror!) OR a shim around the MDIO access (2 more shims). Ugh.

Hmm, so one way or another there's a mirrored signature or a shim. A *deliberate, documented* pair of 2 tiny MDIO shims is the cheapest and avoids any UB: 

```c
/* board glue, one pair, shared by both ports */
static int eth_mdio_read(void *ctx, uint8_t phy, uint8_t reg, uint16_t *val)
{
  return rk3576_gmac_mdio_read(ctx, phy, reg, val);
}
```
Here `rk3576_gmac_mdio_read` takes `void *` too, so the shim is a *cast-free* pass-through — actually then the shim is pointless: if the chip's function already has signature `int(void*, uint8_t, uint8_t, uint16_t*)`, the board can pass it directly and there's no shim, just a naming convention. The "mirror" is that both headers declare compatible prototypes - and we document it in both. That's the pragmatic optimum: 2 prototypes mirrored, documented, and the board's `mdiob` struct literal fills them.

OK. I think I should present this design concisely and let them approve, since it's their architecture call. Key points:
- Yes: `drivers/include/ethernet_phy.h` need not be included by the chip.
- Mechanism: the chip declares plain-`void*` function-pointer hooks in its own config; the PHY module declares plain-`void*` callbacks; the board fills them in. The only duplication is 2 prototype signatures (MDIO read/write), mirrored and documented — no include either way.
- Consequence: the chip loses all PHY register knowledge (including the clause-22 link poll), which is *more* decoupled than my earlier proposal; and `struct phy_desc_s` stays where it is (board-level data) or moves into the PHY module's own descriptor type.

Hmm, `struct phy_desc_s` (NuttX's) — if the PHY module owns probing/IDs, it may want its own struct rather than NuttX's. But keeping NuttX's type is nice (board data in NuttX's vocabulary). The PHY module can consume `struct phy_desc_s` without the chip knowing it. Hmm, but then the module's `probe(desc, mdio)` API takes `struct phy_desc_s` → that's `<nuttx/net/mii.h>`, which both can include freely ✓ (it's core, not a layer). 

So the neutral shared vocabulary = **NuttX core headers** (`mii.h`), which is exactly what both sides already include. That resolves the "shared type" problem without a project-level interface header at all!

So the final shape:
- `struct phy_desc_s` (nuttx/mii.h) = the board→PHY-module description. Chip never sees it.
- The chip's config: `mdio read/write` callbacks? #define GM_PHY_ANER     0x06 /* autonegotiation expansion    */
#define GM_PHY_CTRL1000 0x09 /* 1000BASE-T control           */
#define GM_PHY_STAT1000 0x0a /* 1000BASE-T status            */

/* Register 9's 1000BASE-T bits are *not* where register 10's are, which is the
 * kind of pair that gets written from memory and then read wrong: register 9
 * advertises full duplex in bit 9 and half duplex in bit 10, with bits 11 and
 * 12 choosing master/slave by hand; register 10 reports the partner's choice
 * in bits 11 and 10.
 *
 * Only full duplex is advertised.  The part's own GBESR (register 15) says it
 * is not 1000BASE-T half duplex capable, so advertising half duplex describes
 * a mode that the PHY cannot enter -- and, worse, leaves the line advertising
 * *only* an impossible gigabit mode.
 */

#define GM_PHY_ADV_1000FULL (1 << 9)  /* reg 9 bit 9  */
#define GM_PHY_ADV_1000HALF (1 << 10) /* reg 9 bit 10, not advertised */
#define GM_PHY_LPA_1000FULL (1 << 11) /* reg 10 bit 11 */
#define GM_PHY_LPA_1000HALF (1 << 10) /* reg 10 bit 10 */

/* All four 10/100 modes and the IEEE 802.3 selector.  Pause is deliberately
 * not advertised: the MAC's flow control is not programmed either, and
 * offering a capability the MAC will not honour is worse than not having it.
 */

#define GM_PHY_ANAR_10_100                                     \
  (MII_ADVERTISE_10BASETXHALF | MII_ADVERTISE_10BASETXFULL |   \
   MII_ADVERTISE_100BASETXHALF | MII_ADVERTISE_100BASETXFULL | \
   MII_ADVERTISE_8023)

#define GM_PHY_ADDR_NONE 0xff

/* The vendor register pages and the register that selects them (PAGSR).  Every
 * page includes register 31 as the selector; writing 0 puts the standard IEEE
 * registers 0..15 back.  See the MAE0621A datasheet's register map.
 */

#define GM_PHY_PAGE_STD 0x0000
#define GM_PHY_PAGE_PHY 0xa43 /* PHYCR1 0x18, PHYCR2 0x19, PHYSR 0x1a */
#define GM_PHY_PAGE_LED 0xd04 /* LCR 0x10                            */
#define GM_PHY_PHYCR1   0x18
#define GM_PHY_PHYCR2   0x19
#define GM_PHY_PHYSR    0x1a
#define GM_PHY_LCR      0x10

/* PHYCR1's MDI pair: bit 9 turns manual configuration on, bit 8 then picks MDI
 * (1) or MDIX (0).  Both only take effect across a PHY reset.

#define GM_PHYCR1_MDI_MDI    (1u << 8)

#define GM_PHYCR1_CLEAR_MASK ((1u << 7) | (1u << 6) | (1u << 2) | (1u << 1))

The part-specific half of the PHY was living inside a 2700-line MAC
driver.  Two things made that the wrong shape: the vendor image runs a
dedicated MAE0621A driver for a reason, and the one fault found so far
was a gigabit advertisement this part cannot honour -- knowledge that
belongs to "this PHY", not to "this MAC".  So it moves out, and the two
trees are kept from including each other.

The join is a pair of plain hooks.  rk3576_gmac_config_s holds
phy_init, phy_advertise and an opaque phy_ctx, all declared with `void *`
parameters, and the PHY driver's entry points take `void *` and cast back
inside.  Neither header includes the other; only the board, which already
includes both, assigns them.  A shared interface header would have been
tidier to read and would have forced one tree to depend on the other's
include path, which is the thing this shape avoids.

What moved: the vendor pages and their validated access, PHYCR1's
never-wanted bits (link-down power saving with the PLL off inside it
leaves the copper side silent while MDIO still answers), the forced MDI
mode, and the advertisement -- which is now derived from the part's own
extended status register instead of a constant, so a descriptor cannot
advertise a mode the part cannot enter.

What stayed with the MAC: the management bus, the address walk, the
clause 22 link poll and carrier reporting.  That is what every MAC driver
in the tree does, and this adds no framework on top of it.  The MAC also
now exposes rk3576_gmac_mdio_read/write(int intf, ...) for the PHY driver,
which the board adapts in four lines.

The device tree of the vendor image, and its clock tree, confirmed the
SoC side is already identical to this driver: GMACn_CON is zero, the 125
MHz source is exact, and the RGMII pins are muxed the same way.  The link
is still unverified in NuttX -- the board has only ever linked under its

## 分层落地情况

```
drivers/include/ethernet_phy.h          接口:mdio 回调 + struct ethernet_phy_s + 两个入口点
drivers/drivers/ethernet_phy/
    ethernet_phy.c                      两个入口点的分发(4 行逻辑)

**搬走的**:厂商页及其校验访问、PHYCR1 的四个"绝不该置"的位、强制 MDI、千兆广告。

这一轮的日志把软件侧基本查干净了,而且**纠正了一个误判**。

## 三个结论

**1. 复位是生效的,"reads low" 是误报。**
证据就在同一份日志里:每次 `ifup` 开头 `bmcr = 0x1140`(复位默认值),而上一次 `ifup` 我们写的是 `0x1000`;若复位没执行,BMCR 不可能回到默认值。`EXT_PORT` 在输出方向上不可靠,所以那行检查是假的,已删除,并在注释里写清"真正的证据是 BMCR 回到默认值"。

**2. 软件没有让晶振停振。**
`phycr1 = 0x2118` = 默认值:ALDPS 使能 = 0、ALDPS 关 PLL = 0。也就是说 PHY 内部没有任何省电位把时钟关掉。若晶振真的不起振,原因不在我们写的任何一个寄存器。

**3. `aner = 0x0004` 是"什么都没听见"的铁证。**
ANER bit2 只是本端"支持 next page";**bit0(链路伙伴自协商可用)= 0**,bit3/bit4(并行检测故障、收到页)也全 0。所以对端在任何速率上都没有被听到过。加上 `physr` bit2=0、bit1 不变、`lpa=0`,PHY 的铜缆接收侧完全没有信号。

同时确认 `ctrl1000 0x0200` —— 广告位现在**与 Linux 写的完全一致**。

## 软件侧到此为止,需要一次硬件测量

寄存器层面已经没有任何和"能工作的配置"不同的地方了。剩下的差异只可能在**物理层**,而你有示波器,这一项能一次定死:

**量 RJ45 的 1、2 脚(MDI 发送对,PHY 的 MDIP0/MDIN0)**

- 接口 up、无链路时,自协商期间应看到 **10BASE-T 链路脉冲串**:每个脉冲约 100 ns,每 **16 ms** 左右一串;
- 设置:DC 耦合、2 V/div、5 ms/div、上升沿触发、单次(single)抓;
- **有脉冲** → PHY 在发送,问题在接收/线对/变压器;
- **完全没有** → 发送侧没工作,与"晶振不起振"一致,那就是模拟/时钟域的问题(硬件)。

**顺便请用和 Debian 那次完全相同的方法重测晶振**(AC 耦合、同样的探头接法)。DC 耦合下 10x 探头会把 `XTAL_IN` 的高阻偏置拉到接近 0,看起来就像"没起振"——这个坑我们踩过一次。

```
MAE0621A: bmcr 0x---- bmsr 0x---- phycr1 0x---- phycr2 0x---- physr 0x---- insr 0x---- lcr 0x----
```

`insr` 是**粘滞**的:bit0 = 自协商出错、bit3 = 自协商完成、bit4 = 链路变化。全 0 表示状态机从头到尾没走到任何一步——这和"跑过但失败"是两种不同的故障,处理方向也不同。这个不需要急着烧,先看示波器结果也行。

## 关键:PHY 自己说"我工作异常"

`INSR` bit5 = **PHY Operation Status**,定义是 `1 = Normal Operation,0 = Abnormal`。`insr = 0x0000` 意味着:

- bit5 = 0 → **PHY 报告自身工作异常**;
- bit0/3/4 全 0 → 自协商**没有出错、没有完成、链路没有变化过**,状态机从头到尾没走一步。

这比"没听见对端"更根本:不是听不见,而是它没在跑。

## 和 Linux 的一处真实差异(刚补上)

Linux 的 `phy_init_hw()` 在释放板级复位线之后,还会用 **BMCR bit15 做一次软件复位**,并等它自清(最长约 500 ms),然后再配置。我们只脉冲硬件复位、等 100 ms 就开始写寄存器。如果这颗 PHY 的**内部复位/PLL 序列需要更长时间才完成**,它就会停在"analog 侧没起来、状态机不动、MDIO 照样应答"的状态——和 INSR 的结论完全一致。

已在 PHY 驱动里实现(改动仍在暂存区,未提交):

```
软复位(BMCR bit15) → 轮询自清,最长 500 ms → 再稳定 100 ms → PHYCR1 清理 → 广告 → dump
```

**这个改动本身就是一个决定性测试**,两种结果都有价值:

| 结果 | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| `MAE0621A: reset cleared after N ms, bmcr 0x----` | 复位序列是活的。看 N 多大(可能之前 100 ms 根本不够),再看随后的 `insr` bit5 是否变 1、是否出现 `link up` |
| `MAE0621A: reset bit never cleared (bmcr 0x----)` + `ifup ... Failed` | **用软件证明了 PHY 的复位/时钟域没在跑**。MDIO 由 MDC 驱动所以一直正常,而复位位是寄存器里唯一"必须变化"的位——它不变,就是内部时钟缺失。这条证据可以直接拿去对硬件,不需要示波器 |

## 如果软复位能通过但链路仍不通,我还有这些软件手段

按价值排序,都**不需要**探 MDI:

1. **PHY loopback(BMCR bit14)**:让 PHY 内部把 TX 直接环回 RX,不依赖铜缆。能验证 PHY 数字侧 + RGMII 通路,并看它在 loopback 下是否上报 link。需要一条受控测试路径(临时脚手架)。
2. **MAC loopback(`MAC_CONFIGURATION.LM` bit12)**:完全不经过 PHY,验证我们的 DMA/描述符/缓存/netpkt 数据面。这一项一旦通过,就能把"驱动数据面"和"铜缆"彻底分开——之前从未验证过。
3. **只用软件复位、跳过 GPIO 脉冲**(一次一个变量):如果 GPIO 脉冲让 PHY 停在半初始化,单独软复位可能更干净。
4. **加长硬件复位**(例如 50 ms 低 + 500 ms 稳定):手册只写 ≥72 ms,但晶振起振可能更慢。
5. **读 MMD device 3(PCS)状态**:用 MACR/MAADR 间接访问,拿第二个独立的链路视角。

回答你的问题:**没到万策尽,还剩三条软件路**,而且有一条不需要烧固件。

## 先说一个被我排除的怀疑

我原本怀疑 TXC 门控没打开。查了时钟树:**全部 127 个 gate 都用同一个 `CLK_GATE_SET_TO_DISABLE` 约定**,而 `pclk_gmac` 用的是同一条代码路径、同一组寄存器、照样工作(寄存器能读、版本号正确)。所以 125M 的门控几乎不可能单独关着,这条排除。

## 路 1(不用烧固件):拿到 Debian 下的同一份 PHY 寄存器

这是唯一能判定"`insr` 报 abnormal 到底是不是真的"的办法。把下面**整行**粘贴(一定要一行,因为内核每秒轮询会覆盖 `MDIO_DATA`):

```sh
# GMAC0 上的 PHY0,读标准寄存器 1、9、15 和页 0xA43 的 0x18/0x19/0x1A/0x1D
A=0x2A220200; D=0x2A220204; \
for r in 1 9 15; do busybox devmem $A 32 $((0x70D|(r<<16))) >/dev/null; busybox devmem $D 32 | sed "s/^/reg$r /"; done; \
busybox devmem $D 32 0xA43 >/dev/null; busybox devmem $A 32 $((0x705|(0x1F<<16))) >/dev/null; \
for r in 0x18 0x19 0x1A 0x1D; do busybox devmem $A 32 $((0x70D|(r<<16))) >/dev/null; busybox devmem $D 32 | sed "s/^/pA43:$r /"; done; \
busybox devmem $D 32 0 >/dev/null; busybox devmem $A 32 $((0x705|(0x1F<<16))) >/dev/null
```

判据:

| Debian 下 `pA43:0x1D` | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| bit5 = 1(如 `0x00a8`、`0x0038` 之类) | **"abnormal" 是真的**:同样的硬件在 Linux 下正常、在我们这里不正常,那就还有软件差异可挖 |
| 全 0 | 这个位可能是"读即清"的一次性标志,我这条线索作废,需要换方向 |

顺带它还会给出 Linux 下的 `phycr1/phycr2/physr`——如果和我们读到的 `0x2118 / 0x0823 / 0x1000` 有任何一位不同,那就是答案。

## 路 2(要烧固件):PHY 回环 + 强制 carrier

`BMCR bit14` 让 PHY 在内部把发送数据环回给接收,**完全不走铜缆**。加上驱动临时把 carrier 置真,就可以在板上 `ping` 自己的地址,从而验证 **PHY 数字侧 + RGMII + MAC + DMA/描述符/缓存** 整条数据面。

- 通了 → PHY 与整条数据面都是好的,故障严格局限在铜缆/PCS 侧(硬件问题);
- 不通 → 连内部回环都过不去,**"PHY 内部没运行"就被独立证实**,也和 `insr=0` 对上。

这是不拆板、不用示波器就能验证 PHY 的最后一招,我会把它做成一个受 Kconfig 控制的临时测试路径。

## 路 3(要烧固件):MAC 回环

`MAC_CONFIGURATION.LM` bit12,连 PHY 都不经过,单独验证我们的 DMA/描述符/缓存/netpkt 是否正确。它和路 2 互补:路 3 通过、路 2 不通过 → 问题在 PHY 与 MAC 之间(RGMII/TXC);两条都不通过 → 我们的数据面有 bug。

From: Liu Changjie <liucj1228@outlook.com>

Add exact PHY ID matching and optional 125 MHz CLKOUT configuration
for the Maxio MAE0621A Gigabit Ethernet PHY. Preserve the existing
hardware configuration when the firmware property is absent.

Signed-off-by: Liu Changjie <liucj1228@outlook.com>
Signed-off-by: Andre Przywara <andre.przywara@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Lunn <andrew@lunn.ch>
---

 drivers/net/phy/Makefile |   1 +

 3 files changed, 112 insertions(+)

diff --git a/drivers/net/phy/Kconfig b/drivers/net/phy/Kconfig
index b4ef927fd4a67..eb40276113a57 100644
--- a/drivers/net/phy/Kconfig
+++ b/drivers/net/phy/Kconfig
@@ -298,6 +298,14 @@ config MARVELL_88X2222_PHY
 	  Support for the Marvell 88X2222 Dual-port Multi-speed Ethernet
 	  Transceiver.
 
+config MAXIO_PHY
+	tristate "Maxio Ethernet PHYs"
+	help
+	  Support for Maxio Ethernet PHYs. Currently this driver supports the
+	  MAE0621A Gigabit Ethernet PHY. The driver optionally selects a 125 MHz
+	  clock on the CLKOUT pin while preserving the hardware configuration on
+	  boards which do not request it.
+
 config MAXLINEAR_GPHY
 	tristate "Maxlinear Ethernet PHYs"
 	select POLYNOMIAL if HWMON
diff --git a/drivers/net/phy/Makefile b/drivers/net/phy/Makefile
index 25c4a3c2429f7..9730b8a6fa5b0 100644
--- a/drivers/net/phy/Makefile
+++ b/drivers/net/phy/Makefile
@@ -72,6 +72,7 @@ obj-$(CONFIG_MARVELL_10G_PHY)	+= marvell10g.o
 obj-$(CONFIG_MARVELL_PHY)	+= marvell.o
 obj-$(CONFIG_MARVELL_88Q2XXX_PHY)	+= marvell-88q2xxx.o
 obj-$(CONFIG_MARVELL_88X2222_PHY)	+= marvell-88x2222.o
+obj-$(CONFIG_MAXIO_PHY)		+= maxio.o
 obj-$(CONFIG_MAXLINEAR_GPHY)	+= mxl-gpy.o
 obj-$(CONFIG_MAXLINEAR_86110_PHY)	+= mxl-86110.o
 obj-y				+= mediatek/
diff --git a/drivers/net/phy/maxio.c b/drivers/net/phy/maxio.c
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000..d2cb238956460
--- /dev/null
+++ b/drivers/net/phy/maxio.c
@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only
+/* Driver for Maxio Ethernet PHYs. */
+
+#include <linux/bitops.h>
+#include <linux/module.h>
+#include <linux/phy.h>
+#include <linux/property.h>
+
+#define MAXIO_MAE0621A_PHY_ID		0x7b744412
+
+#define MAXIO_PAGE_SELECT		0x1f
+#define MAXIO_MAE0621A_PHYCR2_PAGE	0xa43
+#define MAXIO_MAE0621A_PHYCR2		0x19
+#define MAXIO_MAE0621A_CLKOUT_125M	BIT(11)
+#define MAXIO_MAE0621A_CLKOUT_ENABLE	BIT(0)
+
+struct maxio_priv {
+	bool clk_out_125m;
+};
+
+static int maxio_read_page(struct phy_device *phydev)
+{
+	return __phy_read(phydev, MAXIO_PAGE_SELECT);
+}
+
+static int maxio_write_page(struct phy_device *phydev, int page)
+{
+	return __phy_write(phydev, MAXIO_PAGE_SELECT, page);
+}
+
+static int maxio_mae0621a_probe(struct phy_device *phydev)
+{
+	struct device *dev = &phydev->mdio.dev;
+	struct maxio_priv *priv;
+	u32 frequency;
+	int ret;
+
+	priv = devm_kzalloc(dev, sizeof(*priv), GFP_KERNEL);
+	if (!priv)
+		return -ENOMEM;
+
+	phydev->priv = priv;
+
+	ret = device_property_read_u32(dev, "maxio,clk-out-frequency-hz",
+				       &frequency);
+	if (ret == -EINVAL)
+		return 0;
+	if (ret)
+		return ret;
+
+	if (frequency != 125000000) {
+		phydev_err(phydev, "invalid CLKOUT frequency %u\n", frequency);
+		return -EINVAL;
+	}
+
+	priv->clk_out_125m = true;
+
+	return 0;
+}
+
+static int maxio_mae0621a_config_init(struct phy_device *phydev)
+{
+	struct maxio_priv *priv = phydev->priv;
+	int ret;
+
+	if (!priv->clk_out_125m)
+		return 0;
+
+	ret = phy_modify_paged_changed(phydev, MAXIO_MAE0621A_PHYCR2_PAGE,
+				       MAXIO_MAE0621A_PHYCR2,
+				       MAXIO_MAE0621A_CLKOUT_ENABLE |
+				       MAXIO_MAE0621A_CLKOUT_125M,
+				       MAXIO_MAE0621A_CLKOUT_ENABLE |
+				       MAXIO_MAE0621A_CLKOUT_125M);
+	if (ret <= 0)
+		return ret;
+
+	return genphy_soft_reset(phydev);
+}
+
+static struct phy_driver maxio_drivers[] = {
+	{
+		PHY_ID_MATCH_EXACT(MAXIO_MAE0621A_PHY_ID),
+		.name		= "Maxio MAE0621A",
+		.probe		= maxio_mae0621a_probe,
+		.config_init	= maxio_mae0621a_config_init,
+		.suspend	= genphy_suspend,
+		.resume		= genphy_resume,
+		.read_page	= maxio_read_page,
+		.write_page	= maxio_write_page,
+	},
+};
+module_phy_driver(maxio_drivers);
+
+static const struct mdio_device_id __maybe_unused maxio_tbl[] = {
+	{ PHY_ID_MATCH_EXACT(MAXIO_MAE0621A_PHY_ID) },
+	{ }
+};
+MODULE_DEVICE_TABLE(mdio, maxio_tbl);
+
+MODULE_AUTHOR("Liu Changjie <liucj1228@outlook.com>");
+MODULE_DESCRIPTION("Maxio Ethernet PHY driver");
+MODULE_LICENSE("GPL");
--

This is an RGMII PHY. However it totally ignores phydev->interface.
There are four values which we require the PHY driver to act on:

	PHY\_INTERFACE\_MODE\_RGMII,
	PHY\_INTERFACE\_MODE\_RGMII\_ID,
	PHY\_INTERFACE\_MODE\_RGMII\_RXID,
	PHY\_INTERFACE\_MODE\_RGMII\_TXID,

Every other RGMII PHY in linux will configure the delays based on
these values. If these values are ignored, bad things will happen.

From what i understand, the delays are currently configured by
strapping. We are going to get into situations where the strapping and
what the MAC requests are different but no errors are reported.  DT
developers are already bad with RGMII delays, and this is just going
to make it worse.

So you have some choices:

1) Implement configuring the delays in the PHY driver

2) Find out how the delays are currently configured and return
   EOPNOTSUPP if the requested configuration is different to the
   current configuration.

3) Always return EOPNOTSUPP for all the RGMII values, and only accept
   PHY\_INTERFACE\_MODE\_NA, which means configuration has been performed
   using some other mechanism, the PHY driver should not change it.

Additionally, my understanding is this PHY will respond to address 0
as a broadcast address. This is not part of 802.3, and always causes
issues. Please ensure this is turned off.

    Andrew

```
The generic PHY DT binding features a clocks property, which describes
the clock input to the PHY. Typically this is a crystal oscillator, so
it works without software interaction. But some boards want to save some
pennies on that part, and let a clock fanout pin from the SoC provide this
clock signal. In this case the PHY probe routine needs to enable this
clock explicitly.

Look for a "clocks" property inside the PHY node and enable that clock,
if one is provided.

This allows boards with a SoC-driven PHY clock to use the PHY. Please
note that without the clock enabled, the PHY will not be detected on the
MDIO bus, so the PHY-ID needs to be explicitly named in the PHY
compatible string:
	compatible = "ethernet-phy-id7b74.4411";

Signed-off-by: Andre Przywara <andre.przywara@arm.com>

@@ -15,6 +16,7 @@

+	struct clk *clk;

@@ -57,6 +59,11 @@ static int maxio_mae0621a_probe(struct phy_device *phydev)

### The 25 MHz PHY reference — crystals, and NC resistors on the PHY clock

`refclko25m_gmac0/1_out`: mux+div in `CLKSEL_CON36` (0x0390) [7]+[6:0] and
[15]+[14:8]; gates in `GATE_CON05` (0x0814) [10] and [11]. The DTB lists
`clocks = <&cru 0x31/0x32>` on the two `phy@1` nodes, which is why this had to
be asked about at all.

The schematic closes it:

- **Each MAE0621A has its own 25 MHz crystal**, on XTAL_IN/XTAL_OUT (pins
  36/37), and both are fitted. Neither PHY takes a clock from the SoC.
- The SoC's 25 MHz outputs are not even routed to the PHYs:
  `ETH0_CLK0_25M_OUT_M0` is `GPIO3_A4`, which the board uses as `IRC_BIN` (IR
  receiver; the vendor DTB also claims it in its `gpio-leds` node, default
  off), and `GPIO2_D6` is not connected to PHY1. So `CLKSEL_CON36` /
  `GATE_CON05` stay untouched, and the DTB's `clocks = <&cru 0x31/0x32>` on
  `phy@1` is inert here.
- The PHY's own `CLKOUT` (pin 35, 125/25 MHz) runs to `GMACn_MCLKINOUT_M0` —
  `GPIO3_B0` for gmac0, `GPIO2_D7` for gmac1 — **through R1901/R1902, both
  marked NC and unpopulated**: the net exists, but it is not connected to the
  SoC pin. That is what makes `clock_in_out = "output"` a fact rather than an
  option — the MAC cannot take its 125 MHz from the PHY and must generate it
  from CPLL (see "The 125 MHz functional clock" above). If those resistors are
  ever fitted, this section and that one both change.

If a future revision drops the crystals, wiring up `refclko25m` is the first
thing to do: forgetting it looks exactly like a dead controller.
